 855    
 856        print("[INFO] Running NTC prefit...")
 857    
 858        # ---------------------------
 859        # Subset to NTC cells (or use all cells if requested)
 860        # ---------------------------
 861        modality_cell_set = set(modality_cells)
 862        meta_subset = self.model.meta[self.model.meta['cell'].isin(modality_cell_set)].copy()
 863
 864        if use_all_cells:
 865            # Use all cells in the dataset
 866            warnings.warn(
 867                "[WARNING] use_all_cells=True: Fitting technical effects on ALL cells. "
 868                "Only use this mode if technical effects are independent of perturbation effects. "
 869                "If technical groups correlate with cis gene expression, "
 870                "use the default NTC-only mode to avoid over-correction.",
 871                UserWarning
 872            )
 873            meta_ntc = meta_subset.copy()  # Use all cells
 874            ntc_cell_list = meta_ntc["cell"].tolist()
 875            ntc_indices = list(range(len(modality_cells)))  # All cell indices
 876
 877            # Subset counts -> ALL cells (no subsetting needed)
 878            counts_ntc_array = counts_to_fit
 879
 880            print(f"[INFO] Modality '{modality_name}': {len(modality_cells)} total cells, using ALL cells for technical fit")
 881        else:
 882            # Standard NTC-only mode
 883            meta_ntc = meta_subset[meta_subset["target"] == "ntc"].copy()
 884
 885            ntc_cell_list = meta_ntc["cell"].tolist()
 886            ntc_indices = [i for i, c in enumerate(modality_cells) if c in ntc_cell_list]
 887
 888            # Subset counts -> NTC
 889            if counts_to_fit.ndim == 2:
 890                counts_ntc_array = counts_to_fit[:, ntc_indices] if modality.cells_axis == 1 else counts_to_fit[ntc_indices, :]
 891            elif counts_to_fit.ndim == 3:
 892                counts_ntc_array = counts_to_fit[:, ntc_indices, :]  # cells are axis 1 for 3D
 893            else:
 894                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected number of dimensions: {counts_to_fit.ndim}")
 895
 896            print(f"[INFO] Modality '{modality_name}': {len(modality_cells)} total cells, {len(ntc_indices)} NTC cells")
 897    
 898        # ---------------------------
 899        # Quality filters per feature
 900        # ---------------------------
 901        if counts_ntc_array.ndim == 2:
 902            feature_sums_ntc = counts_ntc_array.sum(axis=1 if modality.cells_axis == 1 else 0)
 903            # CRITICAL: Sparse matrices return numpy.matrix of shape (n, 1) from sum()
 904            # This must be flattened to 1D to avoid broadcasting issues with masks
 905            from scipy import sparse
 906            if sparse.issparse(counts_ntc_array):

 908        elif counts_ntc_array.ndim == 3:
 909            feature_sums_ntc = counts_ntc_array.sum(axis=(1, 2))
 910        else:
 911            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected number of dimensions: {counts_ntc_array.ndim}")
 912
 913        zero_count_mask = feature_sums_ntc == 0

 916        # --- Per-group zero-count check for negbinom ---
 917        # Two cases need different treatment:
 918        #  - Reference group (group 0) all-zero: baseline expression can't be estimated;

 920        #  - Non-reference group all-zero: fit the feature on the other groups normally;

 922        any_group_zero_mask = np.zeros(len(feature_sums_ntc), dtype=bool)
 923        _negbinom_nonref_patch = {}   # {group_code (int): bool array [T_all]} — applied post-fit
 924        if distribution == 'negbinom' and 'technical_group_code' in meta_ntc.columns:
 925            groups_ntc_codes = meta_ntc['technical_group_code'].values
 926            unique_groups_nb = np.unique(groups_ntc_codes)
 927            if len(unique_groups_nb) > 1 and counts_ntc_array.ndim == 2:
 928                for g in unique_groups_nb:
 929                    g_mask = (groups_ntc_codes == g)
 930                    if g_mask.sum() == 0:
 931                        continue
 932                    if modality.cells_axis == 1:
 933                        group_sums = counts_ntc_array[:, g_mask].sum(axis=1)
 934                    else:
 935                        group_sums = counts_ntc_array[g_mask, :].sum(axis=0)
 936                    if sparse.issparse(group_sums):
 937                        group_sums = np.asarray(group_sums).flatten()
 938                    feat_zero = (group_sums == 0)
 939                    if g == 0:
 940                        # Reference group zero → baseline corrupted → exclude entirely
 941                        n_new = int((feat_zero & ~zero_count_mask).sum())
 942                        if n_new > 0:
 943                            print(f"[INFO] {modality_name}: {n_new} feature(s) excluded — "
 944                                  f"all-zero NTC counts in reference group (baseline can't be estimated).")
 945                        any_group_zero_mask |= feat_zero
 946                    else:
 947                        # Non-reference group zero → fit on other groups, patch this group after
 948                        # Only track features that aren't already excluded for other reasons
 949                        patchable = feat_zero & ~zero_count_mask
 950                        n_patch = int(patchable.sum())
 951                        if n_patch > 0:
 952                            print(f"[INFO] {modality_name}: {n_patch} feature(s) have all-zero NTC counts "
 953                                  f"in non-reference group {g}; will fit on other groups and "
 954                                  f"set alpha_y=1.0 for group {g} after fitting.")
 955                            _negbinom_nonref_patch[int(g)] = patchable
 956
 957        if distribution == 'multinomial':
 958            # counts_ntc_array: [F, N, K] — vectorise over F
 959            totals = counts_ntc_array.sum(axis=2, keepdims=True)  # [F, N, 1]
 960            with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
 961                ratios = np.where(totals > 0, counts_ntc_array / totals, 0.0)  # [F, N, K]
 962            ratio_stds = ratios.std(axis=1)  # [F, K]
 963            zero_std_mask = np.all(ratio_stds == 0, axis=1)  # [F]
 964    
 965        elif distribution == 'binomial':
 966            if denominator is None:
 967                raise ValueError("Binomial distribution requires denominator for variance check")
 968            denom_ntc = denominator[:, ntc_indices] if denominator.ndim == 2 and modality.cells_axis == 1 else \
 969                        denominator[ntc_indices, :] if denominator.ndim == 2 else \
 970                        denominator[:, ntc_indices, :]
 971
 972            groups_ntc_codes = meta_ntc['technical_group_code'].values
 973
 974            # Arrange as [T, N] (features × cells) for vectorised operations
 975            if modality.cells_axis == 0:
 976                numer_all = counts_ntc_array.astype(float).T  # [N, T] -> [T, N]
 977                denom_all = denom_ntc.astype(float).T
 978            else:
 979                numer_all = counts_ntc_array.astype(float)    # [T, N]
 980                denom_all = denom_ntc.astype(float)
 981
 982            valid = denom_all > 0  # [T, N]
 983
 984            # Features where every cell has zero denominator
 985            all_denom_zero = ~valid.any(axis=1)  # [T]
 986            zero_std_mask = all_denom_zero.copy()
 987
 988            # Global PSI std (NaN where denominator is zero)
 989            psi = np.where(valid, numer_all / np.where(valid, denom_all, 1.0), np.nan)  # [T, N]
 990            with np.errstate(invalid='ignore'):
 991                global_std = np.nanstd(psi, axis=1)  # [T]
 992            zero_std_mask[~all_denom_zero] |= (global_std[~all_denom_zero] == 0)
 993
 994            # Per-group boundary checks (vectorised over T)
 995            for g in np.unique(groups_ntc_codes):
 996                g_mask = (groups_ntc_codes == g)
 997                group_numer = numer_all[:, g_mask]  # [T, Ng]
 998                group_denom = denom_all[:, g_mask]  # [T, Ng]
 999                group_valid = group_denom > 0        # [T, Ng]
1000
1001                has_valid = group_valid.any(axis=1)  # [T]
1002
1003                numer_valid_sum = np.where(group_valid, group_numer, 0.0).sum(axis=1)  # [T]
1004                denom_valid_sum = np.where(group_valid, group_denom, 0.0).sum(axis=1)  # [T]
1005
1006                # All PSI=0: valid cells exist but all numerators are 0
1007                all_psi_zero = has_valid & (numer_valid_sum == 0)
1008                # All PSI=1: sum(numer)==sum(denom) (valid since 0<=numer<=denom per cell)
1009                all_psi_one = has_valid & (numer_valid_sum == denom_valid_sum)
1010
1011                zero_std_mask |= ~has_valid | all_psi_zero | all_psi_one
1012        
1013        elif distribution in ("normal", "studentt"):
1014            if counts_ntc_array.ndim != 2:
1015                raise ValueError(
1016                    f"Unexpected dims for distribution '{distribution}': {counts_ntc_array.ndim}"
1017                )
1018
1019            # Arrange as [N, F] (cells × features) for vectorised operations
1020            y_np = counts_ntc_array.astype(float)
1021            y_2d = y_np.T if modality.cells_axis == 1 else y_np  # [N, F]
1022            F = y_2d.shape[1]
1023
1024            groups_ntc_codes = meta_ntc['technical_group_code'].values
1025            unique_groups = np.unique(groups_ntc_codes)
1026
1027            finite_global = np.isfinite(y_2d)            # [N, F]
1028            no_finite_mask = ~finite_global.any(axis=0)  # [F]: True if no finite vals anywhere
1029
1030            # Global NaN-aware std
1031            with np.errstate(invalid='ignore'):
1032                y_2d_nan = np.where(finite_global, y_2d, np.nan)
1033                global_std = np.nanstd(y_2d_nan, axis=0)  # [F]
1034
1035            zero_std_mask = no_finite_mask | (~no_finite_mask & (global_std == 0))
1036
1037            # Per-group all-NaN check: feature excluded if any group has no finite values
1038            all_nan_any_group_mask = no_finite_mask.copy()
1039            for g in unique_groups:
1040                g_mask = (groups_ntc_codes == g)
1041                if not g_mask.any():
1042                    continue
1043                group_finite = finite_global[g_mask, :]  # [Ng, F]
1044                all_nan_any_group_mask |= ~group_finite.any(axis=0)
1045
1046            zero_std_mask = zero_std_mask | all_nan_any_group_mask
1047    
1048        else:
1049            if counts_ntc_array.ndim == 2:
1050                # Handle sparse matrices which don't have .std() method
1051                from scipy import sparse
1052                if sparse.issparse(counts_ntc_array):
1053                    # Sparse matrix: convert to dense for std calculation per feature
1054                    axis = 1 if modality.cells_axis == 1 else 0
1055                    feature_std_ntc = np.array([np.std(counts_ntc_array[i, :].toarray() if modality.cells_axis == 1 else counts_ntc_array[:, i].toarray())
1056                                                for i in range(counts_ntc_array.shape[0 if modality.cells_axis == 1 else 1])])
1057                    zero_std_mask = feature_std_ntc == 0
1058                else:
1059                    # Dense array: use standard method
1060                    feature_std_ntc = counts_ntc_array.std(axis=1 if modality.cells_axis == 1 else 0)
1061                    zero_std_mask = feature_std_ntc == 0
1062            else:
1063                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected dims for distribution '{distribution}': {counts_ntc_array.ndim}")
1064    
1065        only_one_category_mask = np.zeros(len(feature_sums_ntc), dtype=bool)
1066        
1067        if distribution == 'multinomial':
1068            # per-feature categories must be present in *all* technical groups
1069            groups_ntc_codes = meta_ntc['technical_group_code'].values
1070            unique_groups = np.unique(groups_ntc_codes)
1071
1072            F, _, K = counts_ntc_array.shape  # [features, cells, categories]
1073
1074            # Vectorise over F: O(G) passes over [F, N, K] instead of O(F*G) Python loops
1075            shared_present = None  # [F, K] bool
1076            for g in unique_groups:
1077                g_mask = (groups_ntc_codes == g)
1078                if not np.any(g_mask):
1079                    continue
1080                group_counts = counts_ntc_array[:, g_mask, :].sum(axis=1)  # [F, K]
1081                present_g = group_counts > 0                                # [F, K]
1082                if shared_present is None:
1083                    shared_present = present_g
1084                else:
1085                    shared_present &= present_g
1086
1087            if shared_present is None:
1088                n_shared = np.zeros(F, dtype=int)
1089            else:
1090                n_shared = shared_present.sum(axis=1)  # [F]
1091            only_one_category_mask = (n_shared <= 1)
1092
1093    
1094        needs_filtering_mask = zero_std_mask | only_one_category_mask
1095        needs_exclusion_mask = zero_count_mask | needs_filtering_mask | any_group_zero_mask
1096
1097        # Count features that are excluded ONLY for each reason (no overlap)
1098        num_zero_count_only = (zero_count_mask & ~zero_std_mask & ~only_one_category_mask & ~any_group_zero_mask).sum()
1099        num_zero_std_only = (zero_std_mask & ~only_one_category_mask & ~any_group_zero_mask).sum()
1100        num_single_category = only_one_category_mask.sum()
1101        num_group_zero = (any_group_zero_mask & ~zero_count_mask).sum()  # ref-group-zero exclusions only
1102        num_excluded = needs_exclusion_mask.sum()
1103
1104        if num_excluded > 0:
1105            warnings.warn(
1106                f"[WARNING] {num_excluded} feature(s) excluded from fitting: "
1107                f"{num_zero_count_only} zero-count-only, {num_zero_std_only} zero-std, "
1108                f"{num_single_category} ≤1 category present in all technical groups, "
1109                f"{num_group_zero} zero-in-one-group (negbinom only). "
1110                "Alpha set to baseline for excluded features.",
1111                UserWarning,
1112            )
1113    
1114        # ---------------------------
1115        # Subset to features that can be fit
1116        # ---------------------------
1117        fit_mask = ~needs_exclusion_mask
1118        if fit_mask.sum() == 0:
1119            raise ValueError("No features left to fit after filtering!")
1120
1121        # CRITICAL: Convert boolean mask to integer indices for sparse matrix compatibility
1122        # Scipy sparse matrices don't support boolean indexing like dense arrays
1123        from scipy import sparse
1124        fit_indices = np.where(fit_mask)[0]
1125
1126        if counts_ntc_array.ndim == 2:
1127            if sparse.issparse(counts_ntc_array):
1128                # Sparse matrix: use integer indices
1129                counts_ntc_for_fit = counts_ntc_array[fit_indices, :] if modality.cells_axis == 1 else counts_ntc_array[:, fit_indices]
1130            else:
1131                # Dense array: boolean indexing works fine
1132                counts_ntc_for_fit = counts_ntc_array[fit_mask, :] if modality.cells_axis == 1 else counts_ntc_array[:, fit_mask]
1133        else:
1134            # 3D arrays (multinomial) - use boolean indexing
1135            counts_ntc_for_fit = counts_ntc_array[fit_mask, :, :]
1136
1137        denominator_ntc_for_fit = None
1138        if denominator is not None:
1139            if denominator.ndim == 2:
1140                denom_ntc = denominator[:, ntc_indices] if modality.cells_axis == 1 else denominator[ntc_indices, :]
1141                if sparse.issparse(denom_ntc):
1142                    # Sparse matrix: use integer indices
1143                    denominator_ntc_for_fit = denom_ntc[fit_indices, :] if modality.cells_axis == 1 else denom_ntc[:, fit_indices]
1144                else:
1145                    # Dense array: boolean indexing works fine
1146                    denominator_ntc_for_fit = denom_ntc[fit_mask, :] if modality.cells_axis == 1 else denom_ntc[:, fit_mask]
1147            elif denominator.ndim == 3:
1148                denom_ntc = denominator[:, ntc_indices, :]
1149                denominator_ntc_for_fit = denom_ntc[fit_mask, :, :]
1150    
1151        # ---------------------------
1152        # Build tensors for model
1153        # ---------------------------
1154        N = meta_ntc.shape[0]
1155    
1156        if counts_ntc_for_fit.ndim == 2:
1157            if modality.cells_axis == 1:
1158                y_obs_ntc = counts_ntc_for_fit.T   # [T, N] -> [N, T]
1159                T_fit = counts_ntc_for_fit.shape[0]
1160            else:
1161                y_obs_ntc = counts_ntc_for_fit     # [N, T]
1162                T_fit = counts_ntc_for_fit.shape[1]
1163            # Convert sparse to dense for PyTorch tensor creation
1164            if sparse.issparse(y_obs_ntc):
1165                y_obs_ntc = y_obs_ntc.toarray()
1166        else:
1167            y_obs_ntc = counts_ntc_for_fit.transpose(1, 0, 2)  # [T, N, K/D] -> [N, T, K/D]
1168            T_fit = counts_ntc_for_fit.shape[0]
1169    
1170        C = meta_ntc['technical_group_code'].nunique()
1171        groups_ntc = meta_ntc['technical_group_code'].values
1172    
1173        # Detect K (multinomial categories)
1174        K = None
1175        if is_3d_distribution(distribution):
1176            if distribution == 'multinomial':
1177                K = y_obs_ntc.shape[2]
1178    
1179        # ---------------------------
1180        # Build data for priors per distribution
1181        # ---------------------------
1182        if y_obs_ntc.ndim == 3:
1183            if distribution == 'multinomial':
1184                y_obs_ntc_for_priors = y_obs_ntc.sum(axis=2)   # [N, T]
1185            else:
1186                y_obs_ntc_for_priors = y_obs_ntc.sum(axis=2)
1187        else:
1188            y_obs_ntc_for_priors = y_obs_ntc
1189
1190
1191        # Size-factor use only for NB; otherwise ignore
1192        if distribution == 'negbinom' and sum_factor_col is not None:
1193            ntc_sf = modality.sum_factors.loc[meta_ntc['cell'].values, sum_factor_col].values
1194            y_obs_ntc_factored = y_obs_ntc_for_priors / ntc_sf.reshape(-1, 1)
1195        else:
1196            y_obs_ntc_factored = y_obs_ntc_for_priors
1197
1198        # Helper function to extract rows by mask from sparse or dense matrix
1199        # Maintains sparsity until the final computation
1200        from scipy import sparse
1201        def _extract_rows_sparse_safe(matrix, mask):
1202            """Extract rows using mask, handling sparse matrices efficiently."""
1203            if sparse.issparse(matrix):
1204                # Convert boolean mask to integer indices for sparse compatibility
1205                indices = np.where(mask)[0]
1206                # COO matrices don't support indexing - convert to CSR first
1207                if sparse.isspmatrix_coo(matrix):
1208                    matrix = matrix.tocsr()
1209                # Extract subset - stays sparse
1210                subset = matrix[indices, :]
1211                # Convert to dense only for the subset
1212                return np.asarray(subset.toarray() if hasattr(subset, 'toarray') else subset)
1213            else:
1214                # Dense array: use boolean indexing directly
1215                return matrix[mask, :]
1216
1217        if distribution in ('normal', 'studentt'):
1218            baseline_mask = (groups_ntc == 0)
1219            y_baseline = _extract_rows_sparse_safe(y_obs_ntc_factored, baseline_mask)
1220            sigma_hat = np.nanstd(y_baseline, axis=0) + epsilon
1221            sigma_hat = np.where(np.isfinite(sigma_hat), sigma_hat, 1.0)
1222            sigma_hat_tensor = torch.tensor(sigma_hat, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1223        else:
1224            sigma_hat_tensor = None
1225
1226        # ---- Helper: compute robust SD using MAD with SD fallback ----
1227        def _compute_robust_sd(y_data, epsilon, use_nan=False):
1228            """
1229            Compute robust SD using MAD (median absolute deviation) with SD fallback.
1230
1231            MAD is more robust to outliers and heavy tails common in count data.
1232            Falls back to SD when MAD is 0 (e.g., >50% of values equal the median).
1233
1234            Parameters
1235            ----------
1236            y_data : np.ndarray
1237                Data array of shape [N, T]
1238            epsilon : float
1239                Small constant to avoid division by zero
1240            use_nan : bool
1241                If True, use nanmedian/nanstd for NaN-aware computation
1242
1243            Returns
1244            -------
1245            robust_sd : np.ndarray
1246                Robust SD estimate of shape [T]
1247            """
1248            if use_nan:
1249                median_vals = np.nanmedian(y_data, axis=0)
1250                mad = np.nanmedian(np.abs(y_data - median_vals), axis=0)
1251                cell_sd = np.nanstd(y_data, axis=0)
1252            else:
1253                median_vals = np.median(y_data, axis=0)
1254                mad = np.median(np.abs(y_data - median_vals), axis=0)
1255                cell_sd = np.std(y_data, axis=0)
1256
1257            # Convert MAD to SD (scaling factor for normal distribution)
1258            robust_sd = 1.4826 * mad
1259
1260            # Fallback to regular SD when MAD is 0 (e.g., >50% zeros)
1261            robust_sd = np.where(robust_sd > epsilon, robust_sd, cell_sd)
1262
1263            return robust_sd
1264
1265        # ---- mu_x priors per distribution ----
1266        if distribution == 'negbinom':
1267            baseline_mask = (groups_ntc == 0)
1268            y_baseline = _extract_rows_sparse_safe(y_obs_ntc_factored, baseline_mask)
1269            mu_x_mean = np.mean(y_baseline, axis=0)  # [T_fit]
1270
1271            # Compute robust SD using MAD with SD fallback
1272            robust_sd = _compute_robust_sd(y_obs_ntc_factored, epsilon, use_nan=False)
1273
1274            # Convert to SE of mean, with floor at 10% of mean
1275            N_cells = y_obs_ntc_factored.shape[0]
1276            mu_x_sd = robust_sd / np.sqrt(N_cells) + epsilon
1277            mu_x_sd = np.maximum(mu_x_sd, (mu_x_mean + epsilon) * 0.1)  # floor at 10% of mean
1278
1279            mu_x_mean = mu_x_mean + epsilon  # strictly positive for Gamma
1280
1281        elif distribution in ('normal', 'studentt'):
1282            baseline_mask = (groups_ntc == 0)
1283            y_baseline = _extract_rows_sparse_safe(y_obs_ntc_factored, baseline_mask)
1284
1285            # NaN-aware baseline mean
1286            mu_x_mean = np.nanmean(y_baseline, axis=0)  # [T_fit]
1287
1288            # Compute robust SD using MAD with SD fallback (NaN-aware)
1289            robust_sd = _compute_robust_sd(y_obs_ntc_factored, epsilon, use_nan=True)
1290
1291            # Convert to SE of mean, with floor at 10% of |mean| (or 0.1 if mean is ~0)
1292            N_cells = y_obs_ntc_factored.shape[0]
1293            mu_x_sd = robust_sd / np.sqrt(N_cells) + epsilon
1294            mean_floor = np.maximum(np.abs(mu_x_mean) * 0.1, 0.1)
1295            mu_x_sd = np.maximum(mu_x_sd, mean_floor)
1296
1297            # Safety: replace any remaining non-finite with defaults
1298            mu_x_mean = np.where(np.isfinite(mu_x_mean), mu_x_mean, 0.0)
1299            mu_x_sd   = np.where(np.isfinite(mu_x_sd),   mu_x_sd,   1.0)
1300    
1301        else:
1302            # binomial & multinomial: handled with Beta/Dirichlet in the model
1303            mu_x_mean = np.zeros((T_fit,), dtype=float)
1304            mu_x_sd   = np.ones((T_fit,), dtype=float)
1305    
1306        # CRITICAL MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: Use torch.from_numpy() to avoid copies
1307        # torch.tensor() creates a NEW copy, torch.from_numpy() shares memory with numpy array
1308        # Then explicitly delete numpy arrays and move tensors to device
1309        import gc
1310
1311        # Tensors (scalars and small arrays - copy is fine)
1312        beta_o_beta_tensor  = torch.tensor(beta_o_beta,  dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1313        beta_o_alpha_tensor = torch.tensor(beta_o_alpha, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1314        epsilon_tensor      = torch.tensor(epsilon, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1315
1316        # Large arrays: use from_numpy() to share memory, then move to device
1317        mu_x_mean_tensor = torch.from_numpy(mu_x_mean.astype(np.float32)).to(self.model.device)  # [T_fit]
1318        mu_x_sd_tensor   = torch.from_numpy(mu_x_sd.astype(np.float32)).to(self.model.device)    # [T_fit]
1319        del mu_x_mean, mu_x_sd  # Free numpy arrays
1320
1321        if sum_factor_col is not None and distribution == 'negbinom':
1322            sum_factor_np = modality.sum_factors.loc[
1323                meta_ntc['cell'].values, sum_factor_col
1324            ].values.astype(np.float32)
1325            sum_factor_ntc_tensor = torch.from_numpy(sum_factor_np).to(self.model.device)
1326            del sum_factor_np
1327        else:
1328            sum_factor_ntc_tensor = torch.ones(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1329
1330        groups_ntc_tensor = torch.from_numpy(groups_ntc.astype(np.int64)).to(self.model.device)
1331        del groups_ntc
1332
1333        # CRITICAL: y_obs_ntc is the LARGEST array (2.5 GB)
1334        # Ensure it's contiguous numpy array (required for from_numpy)
1335        if not y_obs_ntc.flags['C_CONTIGUOUS']:
1336            y_obs_ntc = np.ascontiguousarray(y_obs_ntc)
1337        y_obs_ntc_tensor = torch.from_numpy(y_obs_ntc.astype(np.float32)).to(self.model.device)
1338        del y_obs_ntc  # Free the 2.5 GB numpy array immediately
1339        gc.collect()  # Force garbage collection
1340
1341        # Precompute invariants once and pass to _model_ntc so they are not recomputed
1342        # on every SVI step (50,000-100,000 calls).
1343        _model_precomp = {}
1344
1345        if distribution == 'negbinom':
1346            _log_sigma_pc = torch.sqrt(
1347                torch.log1p((mu_x_sd_tensor / mu_x_mean_tensor) ** 2)
1348            ).clamp(min=0.1)
1349            _model_precomp['log_sigma_ntc'] = _log_sigma_pc
1350            _model_precomp['log_mu_ntc'] = torch.log(mu_x_mean_tensor) - 0.5 * _log_sigma_pc ** 2
1351
1352        denominator_ntc_tensor = None
1353        if denominator_ntc_for_fit is not None:
1354            if modality.cells_axis == 1:
1355                denom_for_tensor = denominator_ntc_for_fit.T   # [T_fit, N] -> [N, T_fit]
1356            else:
1357                denom_for_tensor = denominator_ntc_for_fit     # [N, T_fit]
1358
1359            # CRITICAL: Use from_numpy() to avoid copy (denominator can be 2.5 GB!)
1360            # Handle sparse matrices first
1361            from scipy import sparse
1362            if sparse.issparse(denom_for_tensor):
1363                denom_for_tensor = denom_for_tensor.toarray()
1364            if not denom_for_tensor.flags['C_CONTIGUOUS']:
1365                denom_for_tensor = np.ascontiguousarray(denom_for_tensor)
1366            denominator_ntc_tensor = torch.from_numpy(denom_for_tensor.astype(np.float32)).to(self.model.device)
1367            del denom_for_tensor  # Free numpy array immediately
1368            gc.collect()
1369
1370        if distribution == 'binomial' and denominator_ntc_tensor is not None:
1371            _ref_m = (groups_ntc_tensor == 0)
1372            if _ref_m.sum() > 0:
1373                _y_sum = y_obs_ntc_tensor[_ref_m].sum(dim=0).float()
1374                _d_sum = denominator_ntc_tensor[_ref_m].sum(dim=0).float()
1375            else:
1376                _y_sum = y_obs_ntc_tensor.sum(dim=0).float()
1377                _d_sum = denominator_ntc_tensor.sum(dim=0).float()
1378            _p_hat = torch.clamp((_y_sum + 0.5) / (_d_sum + 1.0), 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
1379            _kappa = torch.clamp(_d_sum, min=20.0, max=200.0)
1380            _model_precomp['beta_a_precomp'] = _p_hat * _kappa + 1e-3
1381            _model_precomp['beta_b_precomp'] = (1.0 - _p_hat) * _kappa + 1e-3
1382    
1383        # ---------------------------
1384        # Multinomial precomputations (done once, before guide + SVI)
1385        # ---------------------------
1386        if distribution == 'multinomial':
1387            # Replicate the zero-category mask from _model_ntc so we can use it here.
1388            _total_all = y_obs_ntc_tensor.sum(dim=0)                          # [T, K]
1389            _zmask = (_total_all == 0)
1390            for _g in range(C):
1391                _gm = (groups_ntc_tensor == _g)
1392                if _gm.sum() > 0:
1393                    _zmask = _zmask | (y_obs_ntc_tensor[_gm].sum(dim=0) == 0)
1394
1395            # Reference group empirical proportions → log-space init for softmax guide
1396            _ref_m = (groups_ntc_tensor == 0)
1397            _ref_counts = (y_obs_ntc_tensor[_ref_m].sum(dim=0).float() + 1.0
1398                           if _ref_m.sum() > 0 else y_obs_ntc_tensor.sum(dim=0).float() + 1.0)
1399            _ref_counts = _ref_counts.masked_fill(_zmask, 0.0)
1400            _ref_props = _ref_counts / _ref_counts.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
1401            _log_p_init = torch.log(_ref_props.clamp(min=1e-8))              # [T, K]
1402
1403            # Store for the guide closure
1404            self._multinomial_zero_cat_mask = _zmask                         # [T, K]
1405            self._multinomial_log_p_init    = _log_p_init                    # [T, K]
1406            # Reuse precomputed masks/counts in the model to avoid per-step recomputation
1407            _model_precomp['zero_cat_mask_precomp'] = _zmask
1408            _ref_m_multi = (groups_ntc_tensor == 0)
1409            _model_precomp['ref_counts_precomp'] = (
1410                y_obs_ntc_tensor[_ref_m_multi].sum(dim=0).float()
1411                if _ref_m_multi.sum() > 0 else y_obs_ntc_tensor.sum(dim=0).float()
1412            )
1413
1414        # ---------------------------
1415        # Guide + init functions
1416        # ---------------------------
1417        import pyro.poutine as poutine
1418        from pyro.infer.autoguide import AutoNormal, AutoNormalMessenger, AutoIAFNormal
1419        from pyro.infer.autoguide.initialization import init_to_median
1420        
1421        def _safe_simplex_from_counts(total_counts_TK: torch.Tensor, interior_floor=1e-3) -> torch.Tensor:
1422            """
1423            total_counts_TK: [T, K] float
1424            Returns p: [T, K] on the simplex, strictly interior (all entries in (eps, 1-eps)).
1425            """
1426            p = total_counts_TK + 1.0
1427            p = p / p.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
1428            K = p.shape[-1]
1429            eps = interior_floor / K
1430            p = (1.0 - K * eps) * p + eps
1431            p = p / p.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
1432            return p
1433        
1434        def init_loc_fn(site):
1435            name = site["name"]
1436
1437            # Derive local shapes from the actual tensors used in the model
1438            if y_obs_ntc_tensor.dim() == 3:
1439                T_local = int(y_obs_ntc_tensor.shape[1])
1440                K_local = int(y_obs_ntc_tensor.shape[2])
1441            else:
1442                T_local = int(y_obs_ntc_tensor.shape[1])
1443                K_local = None
1444
1445            # -------------------------
1446            # Multinomial-only inits
1447            # -------------------------
1448            if distribution == 'multinomial':
1449                # probs_baseline_raw is guided by the softmax pyro.param directly —
1450                # init_loc_fn is never called for it. Only alpha_logits_y reaches here.
1451                if name == "alpha_logits_y":
1452                    # Initialize with logit-scale differences between groups vs reference
1453                    shape = site["fn"].batch_shape  # [C-1, T_fit, K]
1454                    if len(shape) != 3:
1455                        # Fallback to zeros if unexpected shape
1456                        return torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1457
1458                    Cminus1, T_fit_local, K_local = shape
1459
1460                    # Compute empirical proportions per group
1461                    group_codes_np = groups_ntc_tensor.cpu().numpy()
1462                    y_obs_np = y_obs_ntc_tensor.cpu().numpy()  # [N, T, K]
1463
1464                    # Reference group (group 0) proportions
1465                    ref_mask = (group_codes_np == 0)
1466                    if ref_mask.sum() > 0:
1467                        ref_counts = y_obs_np[ref_mask, :, :].sum(axis=0) + 0.5  # [T, K] with pseudocount
1468                        ref_props = ref_counts / ref_counts.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
1469                    else:
1470                        # Fallback uniform
1471                        ref_props = np.ones((T_fit_local, K_local)) / K_local
1472
1473                    # Initialize alpha for each non-reference group
1474                    alpha_init = np.zeros((Cminus1, T_fit_local, K_local), dtype=np.float32)
1475
1476                    non_ref_groups = sorted(set(group_codes_np) - {0})
1477                    for idx, g in enumerate(non_ref_groups[:Cminus1]):  # Ensure we don't exceed C-1
1478                        group_mask = (group_codes_np == g)
1479                        if group_mask.sum() > 0:
1480                            group_counts = y_obs_np[group_mask, :, :].sum(axis=0) + 0.5  # [T, K]
1481                            group_props = group_counts / group_counts.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
1482
1483                            # Logit-scale difference: log(P_group / P_ref)
1484                            epsilon = 1e-6
1485                            ref_clipped = np.clip(ref_props, epsilon, 1 - epsilon)
1486                            group_clipped = np.clip(group_props, epsilon, 1 - epsilon)
1487                            alpha_init[idx, :, :] = np.log(group_clipped / ref_clipped)
1488
1489                    return torch.tensor(alpha_init, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1490        
1491            # -------------------------
1492            # Other distributions — with binomial and negbinom inits
1493            # -------------------------
1494            if name == "log2_alpha_y":
1495                if distribution == 'negbinom':
1496                    group_codes = meta_ntc["technical_group_code"].values
1497                    group_labels = np.array(sorted(set(group_codes) - {0}))
1498                    init_values = []
1499                    # Use helper to safely extract baseline group (handles sparse matrices)
1500                    baseline_data = _extract_rows_sparse_safe(y_obs_ntc_factored, group_codes == 0)
1501                    baseline_mean = np.mean(baseline_data, axis=0) + 1e-8
1502                    for g in group_labels:
1503                        # Use helper for each group
1504                        group_data = _extract_rows_sparse_safe(y_obs_ntc_factored, group_codes == g)
1505                        group_mean = np.mean(group_data, axis=0) + 1e-8
1506                        init_values.append(np.log2(group_mean / baseline_mean))
1507                    init_arr = np.stack(init_values) if len(init_values) else np.zeros((0, T_local), dtype=np.float32)
1508                    return torch.tensor(init_arr, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1509
1510                elif distribution == 'binomial':
1511                    # Initialize with logit-scale differences between groups (on logit scale)
1512                    group_codes_np = groups_ntc_tensor.cpu().numpy()
1513                    y_obs_np = y_obs_ntc_tensor.cpu().numpy()  # [N, T]
1514                    denom_np = denominator_ntc_tensor.cpu().numpy()  # [N, T]
1515
1516                    # Compute PSI per group
1517                    epsilon = 1e-6
1518
1519                    # Reference group (group 0) PSI
1520                    ref_mask = (group_codes_np == 0)
1521                    if ref_mask.sum() > 0:
1522                        ref_numer = y_obs_np[ref_mask, :].sum(axis=0) + 0.5  # [T] with pseudocount
1523                        ref_denom = denom_np[ref_mask, :].sum(axis=0) + 1.0   # [T] with pseudocount
1524                        ref_psi = np.clip(ref_numer / ref_denom, epsilon, 1 - epsilon)
1525                    else:
1526                        # Fallback uniform
1527                        ref_psi = np.ones(T_local) * 0.5
1528
1529                    # Compute logit of reference PSI
1530                    ref_logit = np.log(ref_psi / (1 - ref_psi))
1531
1532                    # Initialize alpha for each non-reference group
1533                    init_values = []
1534                    non_ref_groups = sorted(set(group_codes_np) - {0})
1535
1536                    for g in non_ref_groups[:C-1]:  # Ensure we don't exceed C-1
1537                        group_mask = (group_codes_np == g)
1538                        if group_mask.sum() > 0:
1539                            group_numer = y_obs_np[group_mask, :].sum(axis=0) + 0.5  # [T]
1540                            group_denom = denom_np[group_mask, :].sum(axis=0) + 1.0   # [T]
1541                            group_psi = np.clip(group_numer / group_denom, epsilon, 1 - epsilon)
1542
1543                            # Logit-scale difference: logit(PSI_group) - logit(PSI_ref)
1544                            group_logit = np.log(group_psi / (1 - group_psi))
1545                            init_values.append(group_logit - ref_logit)
1546                        else:
1547                            init_values.append(np.zeros(T_local, dtype=np.float32))
1548
1549                    init_arr = np.stack(init_values) if len(init_values) else np.zeros((0, T_local), dtype=np.float32)
1550                    return torch.tensor(init_arr, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1551
1552                else:
1553                    return torch.zeros((C - 1, T_local), dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1554        
1555            # Default for everything else
1556            return init_to_median(site)
1557        
1558        pyro.clear_param_store()
1559
1560        # ---------------------------
1561        # Guide choice with memory check
1562        # ---------------------------
1563        if distribution == 'multinomial':
1564            # Softmax guide for probs_baseline_raw: avoids the stick-breaking gradient
1565            # compression that caused AutoDelta to overshoot near the simplex boundary.
1566            # We parameterise log-proportions in ℝ^K and apply softmax — gradients are
1567            # uniform everywhere, no vanishing near p→1.
1568            _zmask_guide  = self._multinomial_zero_cat_mask   # [T, K]  captured in closure
1569            _log_p_init_g = self._multinomial_log_p_init      # [T, K]
1570            _T_guide      = T_fit
1571            _plate_name   = "feature_plate_technical"
1572
1573            # AutoNormal for alpha_logits_y (all sites except probs_baseline_raw)
1574            _guide_alpha = AutoNormal(
1575                poutine.block(self._model_ntc, hide=["probs_baseline_raw"]),
1576                init_loc_fn=init_loc_fn,
1577            )
1578
1579            def ntc_guide(*args, **kwargs):
1580                # ---- probs_baseline_raw: softmax-parameterised point estimate ----
1581                log_p = pyro.param("probs_baseline_logits", _log_p_init_g)  # [T, K]
1582                log_p_masked = log_p.masked_fill(_zmask_guide, -1e9)
1583                probs = torch.softmax(log_p_masked, dim=-1)                  # [T, K]
1584                # Clamp masked categories away from exact 0.0 (float32 underflow of
1585                # softmax(-1e9)).  xlogy(concentration-1, probs) backward = 0/0 = NaN
1586                # when concentration=1 (masked) and probs=0.  Any probs>0 gives finite
1587                # gradient = 0.  1e-30 >> float32 subnormal floor (~1.2e-38).
1588                probs = probs.clamp_min(1e-30)
1589                probs = probs / probs.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
1590                with pyro.plate(_plate_name, _T_guide, dim=-1):
1591                    pyro.sample("probs_baseline_raw", dist.Delta(probs, event_dim=1))
1592                # ---- everything else: AutoNormal ----
1593                _guide_alpha(*args, **kwargs)
1594
1595        elif distribution in ['binomial', 'normal', 'studentt']:
1596            # Calmer guide for these distributions
1597            ntc_guide = AutoNormalMessenger(self._model_ntc, init_loc_fn=init_loc_fn)
1598
1599        else:
1600            # For negbinom and other distributions: check if IAF is feasible
1601            # Estimate number of latent variables
1602            if distribution == 'negbinom':
1603                # log2_alpha_y: (C-1) × T_fit
1604                # o_y: T_fit
1605                # mu_ntc: T_fit
1606                n_latent = (C - 1 + 2) * T_fit
1607            else:
1608                # Conservative estimate for unknown distributions
1609                n_latent = C * T_fit
1610
1611            # IAF memory estimate (rough approximation):
1612            # - Transformation matrices: n_latent × n_latent × 4 bytes (float32)
1613            # - Hidden states: ~2× the matrix size
1614            # - Safety margin: 1.5×
1615            iaf_memory_gb = (n_latent ** 2 * 4 * 3 * 1.5) / 1e9
1616
1617            # Check available VRAM
1618            use_iaf = False
1619            if self.model.device.type == 'cuda':
1620                try:
1621                    # torch is already imported at module level
1622                    total_memory_gb = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(self.model.device).total_memory / 1e9
1623                    # Reserve 10 GB for data, gradients, and other operations
1624                    available_for_guide_gb = total_memory_gb - 10.0
1625
1626                    if force_iaf:
1627                        use_iaf = True
1628                        print(f"[INFO] force_iaf=True: using AutoIAFNormal (estimated {iaf_memory_gb:.1f} GB, "
1629                              f"{available_for_guide_gb:.1f} GB available — OOM risk if estimate is accurate)")
1630                    elif iaf_memory_gb < available_for_guide_gb:
1631                        use_iaf = True
1632                        print(f"[INFO] Using AutoIAFNormal guide (estimated {iaf_memory_gb:.1f} GB < {available_for_guide_gb:.1f} GB available)")
1633                    else:
1634                        print(f"[WARNING] AutoIAFNormal would require ~{iaf_memory_gb:.1f} GB VRAM (>{available_for_guide_gb:.1f} GB available)")
1635                        print(f"[WARNING] Falling back to AutoNormal (mean-field approximation) for {n_latent} latent variables")
1636                        # Increase niters for AutoNormal if using default (AutoNormal needs more iterations)
1637                        if niters_was_default and niters < 100_000:
1638                            old_niters = niters
1639                            niters = 100_000
1640                            print(f"[INFO] Increasing niters from {old_niters:,} to {niters:,} for AutoNormal convergence")
1641                except Exception as e:
1642                    print(f"[WARNING] Could not check VRAM ({e}), using AutoNormal for safety")
1643                    # Increase niters for AutoNormal if using default
1644                    if niters_was_default and niters < 100_000:
1645                        old_niters = niters
1646                        niters = 100_000
1647                        print(f"[INFO] Increasing niters from {old_niters:,} to {niters:,} for AutoNormal convergence")
1648            else:
1649                # CPU: always use AutoNormal for large models
1650                if n_latent > 5000:
1651                    print(f"[INFO] Using AutoNormal for CPU fitting with {n_latent} latent variables")
1652                    # Increase niters for AutoNormal if using default
1653                    if niters_was_default and niters < 100_000:
1654                        old_niters = niters
1655                        niters = 100_000
1656                        print(f"[INFO] Increasing niters from {old_niters:,} to {niters:,} for AutoNormal convergence")
1657                else:
1658                    use_iaf = True
1659
1660            if use_iaf:
1661                ntc_guide = AutoIAFNormal(self._model_ntc, init_loc_fn=init_loc_fn)
1662                # Initialize the guide by calling it once with the model
1663                with torch.no_grad():
1664                    ntc_guide(
1665                        N, T_fit, C,
1666                        groups_ntc_tensor,
1667                        y_obs_ntc_tensor,
1668                        sum_factor_ntc_tensor,
1669                        beta_o_alpha_tensor,
1670                        beta_o_beta_tensor,
1671                        mu_x_mean_tensor,
1672                        mu_x_sd_tensor,
1673                        epsilon_tensor,
1674                        distribution,
1675                        denominator_ntc_tensor,
1676                        K,
1677                        sigma_hat_tensor,
1678                        **_model_precomp,
1679                    )
1680                ntc_guide.to(self.model.device)
1681            else:
1682                # Fallback to memory-efficient AutoNormal
1683                ntc_guide = AutoNormalMessenger(self._model_ntc, init_loc_fn=init_loc_fn)
1684
1685        # Choose ELBO based on guide type
1686        if isinstance(ntc_guide, (infer.autoguide.AutoNormal, infer.autoguide.AutoNormalMessenger)):

1688            elbo = pyro.infer.TraceMeanField_ELBO(num_particles=1)
1689        else:
1690            elbo = pyro.infer.Trace_ELBO(num_particles=1)   # you can bump num_particles later if needed
1691
1692        # Use OneCycleLR scheduler for stable convergence
1693        from torch.optim.lr_scheduler import OneCycleLR
1694        base_lr = lr
1695
1696        # OneCycleLR requires pct_start * total_steps > 1 to avoid ZeroDivisionError.
1697        # With pct_start=0.1, minimum total_steps is 11 (0.1*11-1=0.1>0).
1698        _pct_start = 0.1
1699        _min_total_steps = int(1.0 / _pct_start) + 1  # = 11
1700        _scheduler_total_steps = max(niters, _min_total_steps)
1701
1702        optimizer = pyro.optim.PyroLRScheduler(
1703            scheduler_constructor=OneCycleLR,
1704            optim_args={
1705                # underlying torch optimizer
1706                "optimizer": torch.optim.Adam,
1707                "optim_args": {
1708                    "lr": base_lr,      # initial lr (OneCycle will move it)
1709                    "betas": (0.9, 0.999),
1710                },
1711                # OneCycleLR hyperparameters
1712                "max_lr":          base_lr * 10,  # peak at 10x base_lr
1713                "total_steps":     _scheduler_total_steps,
1714                "pct_start":       _pct_start,    # 10% warmup
1715                "div_factor":      25.0,          # initial_lr = max_lr/25
1716                "final_div_factor": 1e4,          # final_lr = max_lr/1e4
1717            },
1718            clip_args={"clip_norm": 10.0},  # gradient clipping
1719        )
1720
1721        svi = pyro.infer.SVI(self._model_ntc, ntc_guide, optimizer, loss=elbo)
1722        if hasattr(ntc_guide, 'to'):
1723            ntc_guide.to(self.model.device)
1724    
1725        # ---------------------------
1726        # Optimize
1727        # ---------------------------
1728        import math
1729        losses = []
1730        smoothed_loss = None
1731        for step in range(niters):
1732            loss = svi.step(
1733                N, T_fit, C,
1734                groups_ntc_tensor,
1735                y_obs_ntc_tensor,
1736                sum_factor_ntc_tensor,
1737                beta_o_alpha_tensor,
1738                beta_o_beta_tensor,
1739                mu_x_mean_tensor,
1740                mu_x_sd_tensor,
1741                epsilon_tensor,
1742                distribution,
1743                denominator_ntc_tensor,
1744                K,
1745                sigma_hat_tensor,
1746                **_model_precomp,
1747            )
1748            losses.append(loss)
1749            if step % 1000 == 0:
1750                print(f"Step {step} : loss = {loss:.5e}, device: {mu_x_mean_tensor.device}")
1751            # Detect NaN/Inf loss early and give an actionable message
1752            if not math.isfinite(loss):
1753                raise RuntimeError(
1754                    f"fit_ntc: loss became {loss} at step {step}. "
1755                    "This usually indicates numerical instability. Try: "
1756                    "(1) lower learning rate (e.g. lr=1e-4), "
1757                    "(2) check for extreme values in sum_factor, "
1758                    "(3) reduce OneCycleLR peak (pass lr=3e-4 to use a smaller cycle)."
1759                )
1760            if smoothed_loss is None:
1761                smoothed_loss = loss
1762            else:
1763                smoothed_loss = alpha_ewma * loss + (1 - alpha_ewma) * smoothed_loss
1764
1765        # ---------------------------
1766        # Predictive (optionally on CPU)
1767        # ---------------------------
1768        _original_device = self.model.device  # Save exact device (e.g. cuda:6) before any switch
1769        run_on_cpu = self.model.device.type != "cpu"
1770        if run_on_cpu:
1771            if hasattr(ntc_guide, 'to'):
1772                ntc_guide.to("cpu")
1773            self.model.device = torch.device("cpu")
1774    
1775            model_inputs = {
1776                "N": N, "T": T_fit, "C": C,
1777                "groups_ntc_tensor": self._to_cpu(groups_ntc_tensor),
1778                "y_obs_ntc_tensor": self._to_cpu(y_obs_ntc_tensor),
1779                "sum_factor_ntc_tensor": self._to_cpu(sum_factor_ntc_tensor),
1780                "beta_o_alpha_tensor": self._to_cpu(beta_o_alpha_tensor),
1781                "beta_o_beta_tensor": self._to_cpu(beta_o_beta_tensor),
1782                "mu_x_mean_tensor": self._to_cpu(mu_x_mean_tensor),
1783                "mu_x_sd_tensor": self._to_cpu(mu_x_sd_tensor),
1784                "epsilon_tensor": self._to_cpu(epsilon_tensor),
1785                "distribution": distribution,
1786                "denominator_ntc_tensor": self._to_cpu(denominator_ntc_tensor),
1787                "K": K,
1788                "sigma_hat_tensor": self._to_cpu(sigma_hat_tensor),
1789                **{k: self._to_cpu(v) for k, v in _model_precomp.items()},
1790            }
1791        else:
1792            model_inputs = {
1793                "N": N, "T": T_fit, "C": C,
1794                "groups_ntc_tensor": groups_ntc_tensor,
1795                "y_obs_ntc_tensor": y_obs_ntc_tensor,
1796                "sum_factor_ntc_tensor": sum_factor_ntc_tensor,
1797                "beta_o_alpha_tensor": beta_o_alpha_tensor,
1798                "beta_o_beta_tensor": beta_o_beta_tensor,
1799                "mu_x_mean_tensor": mu_x_mean_tensor,
1800                "mu_x_sd_tensor": mu_x_sd_tensor,
1801                "epsilon_tensor": epsilon_tensor,
1802                "distribution": distribution,
1803                "denominator_ntc_tensor": denominator_ntc_tensor,
1804                "K": K,
1805                "sigma_hat_tensor": sigma_hat_tensor,
1806                **_model_precomp,
1807            }
1808    
1809        if self.model.device.type == "cuda":
1810            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
1811        import gc; gc.collect()
1812
1813        # ========================================
1814        # AUTO-DETECT MEMORY AND SET MINIBATCH
1815        # ========================================
1816        minibatch_size, use_parallel = self._estimate_predictive_memory_and_set_minibatch(
1817            N=N, T=T_fit, C=C, nsamples=nsamples,
1818            minibatch_size=minibatch_size,
1819            distribution=distribution
1820        )
1821
1822        # CRITICAL MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: Exclude observation predictions from posterior
1823        # These are enormous ([S, N, T]) and redundant since we already have the data
1824        # Default filter excludes: y_obs_ntc, y_obs (for any distribution)
1825        def default_keep_sites(name, site):
1826            # Exclude all observation-level predictions (huge memory waste)
1827            if name in ('y_obs_ntc', 'y_obs', 'obs'):
1828                return False
1829            # Keep all parameter posteriors (small: alpha, mu, phi, sigma, etc.)
1830            return True
1831
1832        keep_sites = kwargs.get("keep_sites", default_keep_sites)
1833
1834        # CRITICAL: Skip observation sampling during Predictive
1835        # During Predictive, posterior samples of alpha_y can be extreme due to heavy-tailed priors
1836        # This causes NaN/Inf in likelihood evaluation
1837        # We only need parameter posteriors (alpha, mu, phi), not observations
1838        model_inputs_with_skip = model_inputs.copy()
1839        model_inputs_with_skip['skip_obs_sampling'] = True
1840
1841        if minibatch_size is not None:
1842            predictive_technical = pyro.infer.Predictive(
1843                self._model_ntc, guide=ntc_guide, num_samples=minibatch_size,
1844                parallel=use_parallel
1845            )
1846
1847            # Run first batch to get shapes, then preallocate full tensors
1848            posterior_samples = {}
1849            batch_idx = 0
1850            with torch.no_grad():
1851                for i in range(0, nsamples, minibatch_size):
1852                    current_batch_size = min(minibatch_size, nsamples - i)
1853
1854                    # Generate batch
1855                    if current_batch_size < minibatch_size:
1856                        # Last batch might be smaller
1857                        predictive_batch = pyro.infer.Predictive(
1858                            self._model_ntc, guide=ntc_guide, num_samples=current_batch_size,
1859                            parallel=use_parallel
1860                        )
1861                        samples = predictive_batch(**model_inputs_with_skip)
1862                    else:
1863                        samples = predictive_technical(**model_inputs_with_skip)
1864
1865                    # First batch: preallocate full tensors
1866                    if batch_idx == 0:
1867                        for k, v in samples.items():
1868                            if keep_sites(k, {"value": v}):
1869                                v_cpu = self._to_cpu(v)
1870                                # Preallocate: [nsamples, ...] with same dtype/shape as v
1871                                full_shape = (nsamples,) + v_cpu.shape[1:]
1872                                posterior_samples[k] = torch.empty(full_shape, dtype=v_cpu.dtype)
1873                                # Fill first batch
1874                                posterior_samples[k][:current_batch_size] = v_cpu
1875                    else:
1876                        # Subsequent batches: fill in-place
1877                        start_idx = i
1878                        end_idx = i + current_batch_size
1879                        for k, v in samples.items():
1880                            if k in posterior_samples:
1881                                posterior_samples[k][start_idx:end_idx] = self._to_cpu(v)
1882
1883                    batch_idx += 1
1884
1885                    # Clean up after each batch
1886                    del samples
1887                    if self.model.device.type == "cuda":
1888                        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
1889                    gc.collect()
1890        else:
1891            predictive_technical = pyro.infer.Predictive(
1892                self._model_ntc, guide=ntc_guide, num_samples=nsamples,
1893                parallel=use_parallel
1894            )
1895            with torch.no_grad():
1896                posterior_samples = predictive_technical(**model_inputs_with_skip)
1897                if self.model.device.type == "cuda":
1898                    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
1899                gc.collect()
1900    
1901        if run_on_cpu:
1902            self.model.device = _original_device  # Restore exact original device (not generic "cuda")
1903    
1904        for k, v in posterior_samples.items():
1905            posterior_samples[k] = v.cpu()
1906    
1907        # ----------------------------------------
1908        # Reconstruct full α (all original T)
1909        # multiplicative baseline=1; additive baseline=0
1910        # ----------------------------------------
1911        # alpha_y_mul is the Pyro site name; normalise to alpha_y
1912        if "alpha_y" not in posterior_samples and "alpha_y_mul" in posterior_samples:
1913            posterior_samples["alpha_y"] = posterior_samples["alpha_y_mul"]
1914
1915        # C == 1: no group effects were sampled — synthesise trivial posterior entries so
1916        # the reconstruction code below sees consistent shapes.
1917        if C == 1:
1918            _ref_tensor = posterior_samples.get("o_y", posterior_samples.get("mu_ntc"))
1919            _S = _ref_tensor.shape[0] if _ref_tensor is not None else 1
1920            if distribution != "multinomial":
1921                posterior_samples.setdefault("log2_alpha_y", torch.zeros(_S, 0, T_fit))
1922                posterior_samples.setdefault("alpha_y_mul",  torch.ones( _S, 0, T_fit))
1923                posterior_samples.setdefault("delta_y_add",  torch.zeros(_S, 0, T_fit))
1924                posterior_samples.setdefault("alpha_y",      torch.ones( _S, 0, T_fit))
1925            else:
1926                _K_local = K if K is not None else 1
1927                posterior_samples.setdefault("alpha_logits_y",          torch.zeros(_S, 0, T_fit, _K_local))
1928                posterior_samples.setdefault("alpha_logits_y_centered", torch.zeros(_S, 0, T_fit, _K_local))
1929                posterior_samples.setdefault("alpha_y",                 torch.zeros(_S, 0, T_fit, _K_local))
1930
1931        def _reconstruct_full_2d(alpha_fit, baseline_value, fit_mask_bool):
1932            fit_idx = np.where(fit_mask_bool)[0]
1933            if alpha_fit.dim() == 3:           # [S, C-1, T_fit]
1934                S, Cminus1, _ = alpha_fit.shape
1935                full = torch.full((S, Cminus1 + 1, len(fit_mask_bool)),
1936                                  baseline_value, dtype=alpha_fit.dtype, device=alpha_fit.device)
1937                full[:, 1:, fit_idx] = alpha_fit
1938            elif alpha_fit.dim() == 2:         # [C-1, T_fit]
1939                Cminus1, _ = alpha_fit.shape
1940                full = torch.full((Cminus1 + 1, len(fit_mask_bool)),
1941                                  baseline_value, dtype=alpha_fit.dtype, device=alpha_fit.device)
1942                full[1:, fit_idx] = alpha_fit
1943            else:
1944                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected alpha shape: {alpha_fit.shape}")
1945            return full
1946
1947        def _reconstruct_full_3d(alpha_fit, baseline_value, fit_mask_bool):
1948            """
1949            Normalize alpha_fit to [S, C-1, T_fit, K] (S may be 1),
1950            then expand to full [S, C, T_all, K] inserting the baseline row
1951            and placing T_fit back into original T_all via fit_mask_bool.
1952            """
1953            # last two dims must be (T_fit, K)
1954            Tfit = alpha_fit.size(-2)
1955            K_   = alpha_fit.size(-1)
1956            if Tfit != T_fit or K_ != K:
1957                raise ValueError(f"alpha_fit trailing dims mismatch: got (T={Tfit},K={K_}) expected (T={T_fit},K={K})")
1958        
1959            # ----- Step 1: ensure a leading sample dim S -----
1960            t = alpha_fit
1961            if t.dim() == 3:
1962                # [C-1, T_fit, K] -> [1, C-1, T_fit, K]
1963                t = t.unsqueeze(0)
1964            elif t.dim() == 4:
1965                # [S, C-1, T_fit, K] -> OK
1966                pass
1967            elif t.dim() >= 5:
1968                # e.g. [S, 1, 1, T_fit, K] or even [S, a, b, T_fit, K]
1969                # Collapse all dims between S and the trailing (T_fit,K) into a single (C-1) axis.
1970                S = t.size(0)
1971                # product over dims 1..(dim-3)
1972                pre_shape = t.shape[1:-2]
1973                Cminus1 = 1
1974                for d in pre_shape:
1975                    Cminus1 *= int(d)
1976                t = t.reshape(S, Cminus1, Tfit, K_)
1977            else:
1978                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected 3D alpha shape: {tuple(alpha_fit.shape)}")
1979        
1980            # t is now [S, C-1, T_fit, K]
1981            S, Cminus1, Tfit, K_ = t.shape
1982        
1983            # ----- Step 2: build full [S, C, T_all, K] and scatter T_fit back -----
1984            fit_idx = torch.as_tensor(np.where(fit_mask_bool)[0], device=t.device)
1985            full = torch.full(
1986                (S, Cminus1 + 1, len(fit_mask_bool), K_),
1987                baseline_value,
1988                dtype=t.dtype,
1989                device=t.device,
1990            )
1991            full[:, 1:, fit_idx, :] = t  # insert non-baseline rows into fit positions
1992            return full
1993
1994    
1995        if distribution == "multinomial":
1996            # Use the logits that actually entered the likelihood
1997            alpha_logits_fit = (
1998                posterior_samples.get("alpha_logits_y_centered",
1999                                      posterior_samples["alpha_logits_y"])
2000            )  # [S?, C-1, T_fit, K]
2001            alpha_add_full = _reconstruct_full_3d(
2002                alpha_logits_fit, baseline_value=0.0, fit_mask_bool=fit_mask
2003            )
2004        
2005            # Store consistently
2006            posterior_samples["alpha_y_add"]  = alpha_add_full          # [S?, C, T_all, K]
2007            posterior_samples["alpha_y_mult"] = None
2008            posterior_samples["alpha_y"]      = alpha_add_full
2009        else:
2010            # existing path for 2D α
2011            alpha_y_mult_fit = posterior_samples["alpha_y"]
2012            alpha_y_mult_full = _reconstruct_full_2d(alpha_y_mult_fit, baseline_value=1.0, fit_mask_bool=fit_mask)
2013            log2_alpha_fit = posterior_samples["log2_alpha_y"]
2014            alpha_y_add_full = _reconstruct_full_2d(log2_alpha_fit, baseline_value=0.0, fit_mask_bool=fit_mask)
2015
2016            # Patch non-reference zero-count (group, feature) pairs to baseline (negbinom only).
2017            # These features were included in fitting but the zero-count group's alpha_y estimate
2018            # is unreliable (prior-dominated). Overwrite with 1.0 (no technical correction).
2019            # alpha_y_mult_full shape: [C, T_all]; group index matches technical_group_code.
2020            if _negbinom_nonref_patch:
2021                n_pairs = sum(int(m.sum()) for m in _negbinom_nonref_patch.values())
2022                print(f"[INFO] Patching alpha_y=1.0 (mult) / 0.0 (add) for {n_pairs} "
2023                      f"(group, feature) pair(s) with all-zero NTC counts in a non-reference group.")
2024                for g, feat_mask_patch in _negbinom_nonref_patch.items():
2025                    # Use torch LongTensor for feature indices — numpy arrays
2026                    # cause PyTorch to mis-route indices to the wrong dimension.
2027                    # Pyro Predictive always produces a leading S dimension, so
2028                    # _reconstruct_full_2d always returns [S, C, T_all] (3D).
2029                    # The 2D branch [C, T_all] is kept for robustness only.
2030                    # `row` is the non-reference group code (int ≥ 1, < C).
2031                    # `feat_idx_t` indexes T_all, matching the last dimension.
2032                    row = int(g)
2033                    feat_idx_t = torch.as_tensor(
2034                        np.where(feat_mask_patch)[0], dtype=torch.long
2035                    )
2036                    if alpha_y_mult_full.dim() == 2:    # [C, T_all]  — fallback
2037                        alpha_y_mult_full[row, feat_idx_t] = 1.0
2038                        alpha_y_add_full[row, feat_idx_t] = 0.0
2039                    else:                               # [S, C, T_all] — normal
2040                        alpha_y_mult_full[:, row, feat_idx_t] = 1.0
2041                        alpha_y_add_full[:, row, feat_idx_t] = 0.0
2042
2043            # Choose correct type based on distribution
2044            # negbinom: multiplicative, others: additive
2045            if distribution == 'negbinom':
2046                posterior_samples["alpha_y"] = alpha_y_mult_full
2047            else:  # binomial, normal, studentt use additive
2048                posterior_samples["alpha_y"] = alpha_y_add_full
2049
2050            posterior_samples["alpha_y_mult"]  = alpha_y_mult_full
2051            posterior_samples["alpha_y_add"]   = alpha_y_add_full
2052
2053        # ----------------------------------------
2054        # Generic reconstruction of feature-wise posteriors: T_fit -> T_all
2055        # ----------------------------------------
2056
2057        T_all = len(fit_mask)                  # original feature count
2058        T_fit_detected = int(fit_mask.sum())   # number actually fit
2059        # build once, on CPU (safe because all posterior tensors were .cpu()'d)
2060        fit_idx_cpu = torch.as_tensor(np.where(fit_mask)[0], device=torch.device("cpu"))
2061        
2062        def _scatter_T(full_template, t, axis=-1):
2063            index = [slice(None)] * full_template.dim()
2064            index[axis] = fit_idx_cpu.to(full_template.device)  # <-- ensure same device
2065            full_template[tuple(index)] = t
2066            return full_template
2067        
2068        def _reconstruct_feature_axis(x, *, fill_value_nan=True):
2069            """
2070            Detect the feature axis (either -1 or -2 when a trailing K/D exists),
2071            create a full tensor with T_all on that axis, fill with NaN or
2072            zeros (for 'no-effect' defaults), and scatter the T_fit slice back.
2073            Returns reconstructed tensor or the original if no T_fit axis detected.
2074            """
2075            if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor):
2076                return x
2077
2078            # figure out where T_fit lives
2079            axis = None
2080            if x.dim() >= 1 and x.shape[-1] == T_fit_detected:
2081                axis = -1
2082            elif x.dim() >= 2 and x.shape[-2] == T_fit_detected:
2083                axis = -2
2084
2085            if axis is None:
2086                return x  # not a feature-wise tensor, skip
2087
2088            # shape with T_all inserted
2089            full_shape = list(x.shape)
2090            full_shape[axis] = T_all
2091
2092            if fill_value_nan:
2093                fill_val = torch.tensor(float('nan'), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
2094            else:
2095                fill_val = torch.tensor(0.0, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
2096
2097            full = torch.full(full_shape, fill_val, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
2098            return _scatter_T(full, x, axis=axis)
2099
2100        # Decide which keys are "effects" (fill with 0.0) vs "baselines/scales" (fill with NaN)
2101        # You can extend/tweak these sets as your model grows.
2102        effect_like_keys = {
2103            # common across dists
2104            "log2_alpha_y", "delta_y_add", "alpha_y_mul",  # raw effect params
2105            # multinomial logits
2106            "alpha_logits_y", "alpha_logits_y_centered",
2107        }
2108
2109        baseline_like_keys = {
2110            # NB / Normal / Binomial baselines & variances
2111            "mu_ntc", "o_y", "sigma_y",
2112            # MVN
2113            "mu_ntc_mv", "sigma_y_mv",
2114            # Multinomial baseline probs
2115            "probs_baseline",
2116        }
2117
2118        # α’s already reconstructed above; skip final forms to avoid double work
2119        skip_keys = {
2120            "alpha_y", "alpha_y_mult", "alpha_y_add"
2121        }
2122
2123        # Reconstruct any posterior that carries T_fit
2124        for k, v in list(posterior_samples.items()):
2125            if k in skip_keys:
2126                continue
2127            if not isinstance(v, torch.Tensor):
2128                continue
2129
2130            # Heuristic: only attempt if a T_fit-looking axis exists
2131            has_Tfit_axis = (
2132                (v.dim() >= 1 and v.shape[-1] == T_fit_detected) or
2133                (v.dim() >= 2 and v.shape[-2] == T_fit_detected)
2134            )
2135            if not has_Tfit_axis:
2136                continue
2137
2138            # Choose fill: 0.0 for effect-like, NaN for baseline-like (default)
2139            fill_nan = k not in effect_like_keys
2140            try:
2141                posterior_samples[k] = _reconstruct_feature_axis(v, fill_value_nan=fill_nan)
2142            except Exception as e:
2143                print(f"[WARN] Skipped reconstruction for '{k}' due to: {e}")
2144        
2145        # ----------------------------------------
2146        # Feature metadata flags
2147        # ----------------------------------------
2148        # Masks cover rows 0..n_trans_features-1 (trans genes) and optionally
2149        # row n_trans_features (cis gene, if appended).  Store only the trans
2150        # portion in the modality's feature_meta.
2151        if len(modality.feature_meta) == n_trans_features:
2152            modality.feature_meta["ntc_zero_count"]               = zero_count_mask[:n_trans_features].tolist()
2153            modality.feature_meta["ntc_zero_std"]                 = zero_std_mask[:n_trans_features].tolist()
2154            modality.feature_meta["ntc_single_category"]          = only_one_category_mask[:n_trans_features].tolist()
2155            modality.feature_meta["ntc_excluded_from_fit"]        = needs_exclusion_mask[:n_trans_features].tolist()
2156            modality.feature_meta["technical_correction_applied"] = (~needs_exclusion_mask[:n_trans_features]).tolist()
2157
2158    
2159        # ----------------------------------------
2160        # Persist results at modality level
2161        # ----------------------------------------
2162        if cis_idx_in_counts is not None:
2163            # Cis gene was appended as the last row.  Extract its alpha for alpha_x_prefit,
2164            # then trim it from all primary-modality posteriors so they align with the modality.
2165
2166            if distribution == 'multinomial':
2167                raise ValueError(
2168                    "Primary modality uses a multinomial distribution, "
2169                    "but cis effect extraction is undefined for multinomial. "
2170                    "Ensure the primary modality is not multinomial when cis is present."
2171                )
2172
2173            full_alpha_y_mult = posterior_samples["alpha_y_mult"]
2174            full_alpha_y_add  = posterior_samples["alpha_y_add"]
2175
2176            if full_alpha_y_mult is None:
2177                raise RuntimeError(
2178                    "alpha_y_mult is None while attempting cis extraction. "
2179                    "This can happen if the distribution is multinomial; "
2180                    "check distribution handling earlier."
2181                )
2182
2183            cis_idx_orig = cis_idx_in_counts          # always == n_trans_features
2184            trans_idx    = list(range(cis_idx_orig))  # 0 .. n_trans_features-1
2185            T_all_with_cis = n_trans_features + 1
2186
2187            # alpha_x_prefit: median over posterior samples → [C]
2188            self.model.alpha_x_prefit = full_alpha_y_mult[..., cis_idx_orig].median(dim=0).values
2189
2190            # Modality alpha_y: trans genes only → median → [C, T]
2191            if modality.distribution == 'negbinom':
2192                modality.alpha_y_prefit_mult = full_alpha_y_mult[..., trans_idx].median(dim=0).values
2193            else:
2194                modality.alpha_y_prefit_add = full_alpha_y_add[..., trans_idx].median(dim=0).values
2195
2196            # ---- Store cis gene posteriors in cis modality ----
2197            cis_modality = self.model.get_modality('cis')
2198            cis_posterior = {}
2199            for src_key, dst_key in [
2200                ('log2_alpha_y', 'log2_alpha_x'), ('alpha_y_mul', 'alpha_x_mul'),
2201                ('delta_y_add', 'delta_x_add'),   ('o_y',         'o_x'),
2202                ('mu_ntc',      'mu_ntc'),
2203            ]:
2204                if src_key in posterior_samples:
2205                    cis_posterior[dst_key] = posterior_samples[src_key][..., cis_idx_orig:cis_idx_orig+1]
2206
2207            if 'alpha_x_mul' in cis_posterior:
2208                raw = cis_posterior['alpha_x_mul']  # [S, C-1, 1]
2209                if raw.dim() == 3:
2210                    S, Cminus1, _ = raw.shape
2211                    cis_posterior['alpha_x_mult'] = torch.cat(
2212                        [torch.ones(S, 1, 1, device=raw.device), raw], dim=1)
2213                    cis_posterior['alpha_x'] = cis_posterior['alpha_x_mult']
2214
2215            if 'delta_x_add' in cis_posterior:

2217                if raw.dim() == 3:
2218                    S, Cminus1, _ = raw.shape
2219                    cis_posterior['alpha_x_add'] = torch.cat(
2220                        [torch.zeros(S, 1, 1, device=raw.device), raw], dim=1)
2221
2222            cis_modality.posterior_samples_ntc = cis_posterior
2223            print(f"[INFO] Stored cis gene posteriors in 'cis' modality: {list(cis_posterior.keys())}")

2225            # ---- Trim cis gene from ALL primary-modality posteriors ----
2226            if modality.distribution == 'negbinom':
2227                posterior_samples["alpha_y_mult"] = full_alpha_y_mult[..., trans_idx]
2228                posterior_samples["alpha_y"]      = posterior_samples["alpha_y_mult"]
2229            else:
2230                posterior_samples["alpha_y_add"] = full_alpha_y_add[..., trans_idx]
2231                posterior_samples["alpha_y"]     = posterior_samples["alpha_y_add"]
2232
2233            for key in ['log2_alpha_y', 'alpha_y_mul', 'delta_y_add', 'o_y', 'mu_ntc']:
2234                if key in posterior_samples and isinstance(posterior_samples[key], torch.Tensor):
2235                    v = posterior_samples[key]
2236                    if v.shape[-1] == T_all_with_cis:
2237                        posterior_samples[key] = v[..., trans_idx]
2238
2239            print(f"[INFO] Extracted alpha_x for '{self.model.cis_gene}' (index {cis_idx_orig}) "
2240                  f"and trimmed it from primary modality posteriors")

2242        else:
2243            # No cis gene appended (non-primary modality, or no cis_gene set)
2244            if modality.distribution == 'negbinom':
2245                modality.alpha_y_prefit_mult = posterior_samples["alpha_y_mult"].median(dim=0).values
2246            else:
2247                modality.alpha_y_prefit_add = posterior_samples["alpha_y_add"].median(dim=0).values
2248
2249        modality.posterior_samples_ntc = posterior_samples
2250

2253

2255        modality.loss_ntc = losses
2256
2257        print(f"[INFO] Stored technical fit results in modality '{modality_name}'")

2264        print("Finished fit_ntc.")

Estimate technical batch effects and per-gene overdispersion from NTC cells.

Fits a Bayesian negative-binomial model to NTC (non-targeting control) cells, estimating multiplicative cell-line/batch scale factors (alpha_y_mult) and additive logit-scale corrections (alpha_y_add) per technical group. Results are stored on the primary modality as point estimates and are used by fit_trans() to correct for batch effects.

Call set_technical_groups() before this method.

Parameters

sum_factor_col : str, default 'sum_factor' Column in meta (or the primary modality's sum_factors DataFrame) containing size factors for normalisation. lr : float, default 1e-3 Adam optimiser learning rate for SVI. niters : int, optional Number of SVI iterations. Default: 50,000 for most distributions; 100,000 for multinomial (which has a larger parameter space). nsamples : int, default 1000 Number of posterior samples drawn after SVI for point-estimate summaries. alpha_ewma : float, default 0.05 Smoothing weight for the exponential moving average of the ELBO loss used in convergence checking. Smaller values give a smoother (but slower- reacting) estimate. beta_o_beta : float, default 3 Beta parameter of the Gamma prior on the overdispersion o_y. Matches the cell2location prior; change with care. beta_o_alpha : float, default 9 Alpha parameter of the Gamma prior on o_y. Matches the cell2location prior; change with care. epsilon : float, default 1e-6 Small constant added for numerical stability. minibatch_size : int, optional Number of features to use per Predictive minibatch when sampling posteriors. If None (default), auto-computed from available RAM via psutil. distribution : str, optional Likelihood distribution. If None (default), auto-detected from the modality (e.g., 'negbinom', 'multinomial', 'binomial'). denominator : np.ndarray, optional Denominator array for binomial distributions. If None, auto-detected from the modality. modality_name : str, optional Modality to fit. If None (default), uses the primary modality. use_all_cells : bool, default False If False (default): fit using NTC cells only (standard approach). If True: fit using all cells, regardless of target.

**When to use** ``use_all_cells=True``:

- High-MOI experiments where batch effects are independent of perturbation.
- When a single technical fit covers all cis genes (saves compute).

**When NOT to use** ``use_all_cells=True``:

- Technical groups correlate with cis expression (e.g., different cell
  lines have different perturbation efficiencies).
- Low-MOI experiments with a clear NTC vs. perturbed cell distinction.

force_iaf : bool, default False If True, force use of an IAF (Inverse Autoregressive Flow) guide for multinomial models regardless of the number of categories. By default, IAF is only used when the number of categories exceeds a threshold.

Warnings

Using use_all_cells=True when technical effects correlate with cis expression can lead to over-correction and spurious trans-effect calls.

def fit_cis(self, *args, force: bool = False, **kwargs):

1686                        f"Call plot_ntc_expression() to inspect, or pass force=True to proceed anyway."
1687                    )
