2841                    for k, v in samples.items():
2842                        if keep_sites(k, {"value": v}):
2843                            all_samples[k].append(self._to_cpu(v))
2844                    if self.model.device.type == "cuda":
2845                        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
2846                    import gc
2847                    gc.collect()
2848
2849            posterior_samples_y = {k: torch.cat(v, dim=0) for k, v in all_samples.items()}
2850
2851        else:
2852            predictive_y = pyro.infer.Predictive(
2853                self._model_y,
2854                guide=guide_y,
2855                num_samples=nsamples
2856            )
2857            with torch.no_grad():
2858                _raw_samples = predictive_y(**predictive_model_inputs)
2859                # keep_sites filters out y_obs (never used downstream, and not computed
2860                # when latents_only=True anyway — this is a safety net for other callers).
2861                posterior_samples_y = {
2862                    k: v for k, v in _raw_samples.items()
2863                    if keep_sites(k, {"value": v})
2864                }
2865                del _raw_samples
2866                if self.model.device.type == "cuda":
2867                    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
2868                import gc
2869                gc.collect()
2870
2871        if run_on_cpu:
2872            self.model.device = _original_device  # Restore exact original device (not generic "cuda")
2873            print("[INFO] Reset self.model.device to:", self.model.device)
2874
2875        for k, v in posterior_samples_y.items():
2876            posterior_samples_y[k] = self._to_cpu(v)
2877
2878        # ----------------------------------------
2879        # Store nmin/nmax and check boundaries
2880        # ----------------------------------------
2881        posterior_samples_y['nmin'] = self._to_cpu(nmin)
2882        posterior_samples_y['nmax'] = self._to_cpu(nmax)
2883
2884        # Warn if fitted n_a parameters are close to boundaries
2885        if 'n_a' in posterior_samples_y and function_type in ['single_hill', 'additive_hill', 'nested_hill']:
2886            n_a_samples = posterior_samples_y['n_a']  # Shape: [S, T]
2887            nmin_val = nmin.item()
2888            nmax_val = nmax.item()
2889
2890            # Define "close to boundary" threshold (e.g., within 10% of range)
2891            boundary_threshold = 0.1 * (nmax_val - nmin_val)
2892
2893            # Check how many samples are close to boundaries
2894            close_to_min = (n_a_samples < (nmin_val + boundary_threshold)).float().mean().item()
2895            close_to_max = (n_a_samples > (nmax_val - boundary_threshold)).float().mean().item()
2896
2897            # Warn if >10% of samples are at boundaries
2898            if close_to_min > 0.1:
2899                warnings.warn(
2900                    f"[WARNING] {close_to_min*100:.1f}% of n_a samples are close to lower boundary (nmin={nmin_val:.2f}). "
2901                    f"Consider: (1) checking if x_true range is appropriate, or (2) relaxing nmin constraint.",
2902                    UserWarning
2903                )
2904            if close_to_max > 0.1:
2905                warnings.warn(
2906                    f"[WARNING] {close_to_max*100:.1f}% of n_a samples are close to upper boundary (nmax={nmax_val:.2f}). "
2907                    f"Consider: (1) checking if x_true range is appropriate, or (2) relaxing nmax constraint.",
2908                    UserWarning
2909                )
2910
2911            # Summary statistics
2912            print(f"[INFO] n_a boundary check: nmin={nmin_val:.2f}, nmax={nmax_val:.2f}")
2913            print(f"[INFO]   {close_to_min*100:.1f}% of samples near lower bound, {close_to_max*100:.1f}% near upper bound")
2914
2915        # ── Compute and save prior parameters for diagnostic plotting ─────────
2916        # These let plot_parameter_ci_panel overlay prior distributions as violins
2917        trans_prior_params = None
2918        if function_type in ['single_hill', 'additive_hill']:
2919            _K_log_sigma_min_val = float(k_log_sigma_min_tensor.item())  # parameterized, default 5*ln(2)/2 ≈ 1.733
2920
2921            # n prior: unconstrained mean (maps to n_mu=0 in constrained space)
2922            _half_n_p   = 0.5 * (nmax - nmin).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
2923            _center_n_p = 0.5 * (nmax + nmin)
2924            _ratio_n_p  = ((n_mu_tensor - _center_n_p) / _half_n_p).clamp(-1 + 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
2925            n_mu_raw_prior = float((_half_n_p * torch.atanh(_ratio_n_p)).item())
2926
2927            # Vmax prior (log-normal): Vmax_log_sigma is the same for all genes
2928            # because sigma/mean = 1/sqrt(Vmax_alpha) regardless of Vmax_mean.
2929            # Apply the same floor that _model_y uses (parameterized via vmax_log_sigma_floor).
2930            if distribution not in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
2931                Vmax_alpha_val   = float(Vmax_alpha_tensor.item())
2932                _Vmax_log_sigma_floor_p = float(vmax_log_sigma_floor_tensor.item())
2933                Vmax_log_sigma_p = max(
2934                    float(np.sqrt(np.log1p(1.0 / Vmax_alpha_val))),
2935                    _Vmax_log_sigma_floor_p,
2936                )
2937                Vmax_log_mu_p    = (np.log(np.maximum(Vmax_mean_tensor.cpu().numpy(), 1e-12))
2938                                    - 0.5 * Vmax_log_sigma_p ** 2)  # [T]
2939            else:
2940                Vmax_log_sigma_p = None
2941                Vmax_log_mu_p    = None
2942
2943            # K prior (log-normal): median centred at x_ntc_mean or k_center fallback.
2944            # K_log_mu = log(centre) with no -0.5*sigma² correction, so the MEDIAN of
2945            # K_a equals the centre (log2FC = 0 for the NTC-centred case).
2946            if x_ntc_mean is not None:
2947                K_log_sigma_p = _K_log_sigma_min_val
2948                K_log_mu_p    = float(torch.log(x_ntc_mean.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)).item())
2949            else:
2950                _K_mean_p  = k_center_tensor.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
2951                _K_std_p   = (_K_mean_p * x_true_CV if x_true_CV is not None
2952                              else K_max_tensor / (2.0 * torch.sqrt(K_alpha_tensor)))
2953                _ratio_K_p = (_K_std_p / _K_mean_p).clamp_min(self._t(1e-6))
2954                K_log_sigma_p = float(torch.sqrt(torch.log1p(_ratio_K_p ** 2))
2955                                      .clamp_min(self._t(_K_log_sigma_min_val)).item())
2956                K_log_mu_p    = float(torch.log(_K_mean_p).item())
2957
2958            trans_prior_params = {
2959                'function_type':    function_type,
2960                'distribution':     distribution,
2961                # n_a / n_b
2962                'nmin':             float(nmin.item()),
2963                'nmax':             float(nmax.item()),
2964                'n_mu_raw':         n_mu_raw_prior,
2965                'sigma_n_prior_rate': 1.0,           # Exp(1) prior per gene → mean sigma = 1
2966                # Vmax_a / Vmax_b (log-normal)
2967                'Vmax_log_mu':      Vmax_log_mu_p,   # [T] numpy array or None
2968                'Vmax_log_sigma':   Vmax_log_sigma_p, # scalar or None
2969                # K_a / K_b (log-normal)
2970                'K_log_mu':         K_log_mu_p,      # scalar
2971                'K_log_sigma':      K_log_sigma_p,   # scalar
2972                # A prior (negbinom: log2-Normal; others: None)
2973                # A_log2_mu / A_log2_sigma: per-gene anchors in log2 space, matching _model_y.
2974                # mu = lower anchor (log2(Amean/2), capped so sigma ≤ 4 octaves).
2975                # sigma = log2(y_ntc) - lower_anchor, clamped to [1, 4] octaves.
2976                # Without y_ntc: sigma = 4 (flat fallback), mu = log2(Amean/2).
2977                'Amean':            (Amean_tensor.cpu().numpy()
2978                                     if distribution not in ['binomial', 'multinomial']
2979                                     else None),      # [T] or None (binomial/multinomial: not applicable)
2980                'A_log2_mu':        None,             # [T] or None — set below for negbinom
2981                'A_log2_sigma':     None,             # [T] or None — set below for negbinom
2982                # alpha / beta (RelaxedBernoulli)
2983                'p_n_logits':       float(p_n_logits_tensor.item()),
2984                'temperature_prior': 1.0,
2985            }
2986
2987            # Fill A_log2_mu / A_log2_sigma for negbinom (matches _model_y lines 658-671).
2988            # Replicate the exact weight used inside _model_y so the violin is accurate.
2989            if distribution == 'negbinom':
2990                _Amean_np = Amean_tensor.cpu().numpy()
2991                if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
2992                    _y_ntc_np = y_ntc_tensor.cpu().numpy()
2993                    # Mirror _model_y: lift upper anchor to mean(y_corrected) when y_ntc < mean.
2994                    if mean_y_corrected_tensor is not None:
2995                        _mean_ycorr_np = mean_y_corrected_tensor.cpu().numpy()
2996                        _upper_np = np.maximum(_y_ntc_np, _mean_ycorr_np)
2997                    else:
2998                        _upper_np = _y_ntc_np
2999                    _log2_upper = np.log2(np.maximum(_upper_np, 1e-12))
3000                    _log2_lower = np.maximum(
3001                        np.log2(np.maximum(_Amean_np / 2.0, 1e-12)),
3002                        _log2_upper - 4.0,
3003                    )
3004                    _sigma_log2_A = np.clip(_log2_upper - _log2_lower, 1.0, 4.0)
3005                    if o_y_ntc_tensor is not None:
3006                        _prior_mean_oy = float((beta_o_beta_tensor / beta_o_alpha_tensor)
3007                                               .clamp_min(epsilon_tensor).item())
3008                        _w = (o_y_ntc_tensor / (o_y_ntc_tensor + _prior_mean_oy)).cpu().numpy()
3009                    else:
3010                        _w = np.zeros_like(_Amean_np)
3011                    _mu_log2_A = (1.0 - _w) * _log2_lower + _w * _log2_upper
3012                else:
3013                    _mu_log2_A    = np.log2(np.maximum(_Amean_np / 2.0, 1e-12))
3014                    _sigma_log2_A = np.full_like(_mu_log2_A, 4.0)
3015                trans_prior_params['A_log2_mu']    = _mu_log2_A    # [T]
3016                trans_prior_params['A_log2_sigma'] = _sigma_log2_A  # [T]
3017
3018        # Store results
3019        # Store in modality
3020        modality.posterior_samples_trans = posterior_samples_y
3021        modality.trans_prior_params = trans_prior_params
3022        modality.losses_trans = self.losses_trans  # Store loss history
3023
3024        # For primary modality, also store at model level for direct access via model.posterior_samples_trans
3025        if modality_name == self.model.primary_modality:
3026            self.model.posterior_samples_trans = posterior_samples_y
3027            self.model.losses_trans = self.losses_trans
3028            self.model.trans_prior_params = trans_prior_params
3029            # NOTE: alpha_y_prefit is stored per-modality (already done above), not at model level
3030            print(f"[INFO] Stored results in modality '{modality_name}' and at model level (primary modality)")
3031        else:
3032            print(f"[INFO] Stored results in modality '{modality_name}'")
3033
3034        if self.model.device.type == "cuda":
3035            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
3036        import gc
3037        gc.collect()
3038        pyro.clear_param_store()
3039
3040        # Remove the rolling checkpoint (_latest.pt) and its temporaries now that
3041        # results are stored on the model.  Numbered (_step*.pt), warmup, and
3042        # complete checkpoints are retained for post-hoc analysis.
3043        if checkpoint_path is not None and not _predictive_only_mode:
3044            for _p in [checkpoint_path, checkpoint_path + '.bak', checkpoint_path + '.tmp']:
3045                if os.path.exists(_p):
3046                    os.remove(_p)
3047            print(f"[INFO] Rolling checkpoint removed; "
3048                  f"numbered/warmup/complete checkpoints retained in "
3049                  f"{os.path.dirname(checkpoint_path)}")
3050
3051        print("Finished fit_trans.")

Fit trans effects using distribution-specific likelihood.

Parameters

modality_name : str, optional Name of modality to fit. If None, uses primary modality. distribution : str, optional Distribution type: 'negbinom', 'multinomial', 'binomial', 'normal' If None, auto-detected from modality. sum_factor_col : str, optional Sum factor column name. Required for negbinom, ignored for others. denominator : np.ndarray, optional Denominator array for binomial distribution (e.g., total counts for PSI) If None, auto-detected from modality. min_denominator : int, optional Minimum denominator value for binomial observations. Observations where denominator < min_denominator are masked (excluded from fitting). Useful for filtering low-coverage splicing junctions. Default: None (no filtering). use_epsilon : bool, optional If True, add 1e-8 epsilon for numerical stability in NegativeBinomial logits. If False (default), use log(mu) - log(phi) directly. warmup : bool, optional For additive_hill/nested_hill: run a single_hill warmup phase before the main fit. Default True (warmup is on by default for additive/nested hill). Ignored for single_hill and polynomial. warmup_T_min : float, optional Temperature at which Phase 1 (single_hill warmup) ends. Phase 1 cools from init_temp down to warmup_T_min at the same rate as Phase 2, so the number of warmup steps is computed automatically: warmup_steps = round(niters * (init_temp - warmup_T_min) / (init_temp - final_temp)) niters always refers to Phase 2 (additive_hill) steps; total steps = warmup_steps + niters. Default 0.5 (roughly half the annealing range, saves ~44% of a full single_hill run while still reaching the separation point where active and null genes are clearly distinguished). vmax_log_sigma_floor : float, optional Minimum log-sigma for the Vmax LogNormal prior (negbinom only). The data-driven log-sigma (≈ sqrt(log(1 + 1/Vmax_alpha))) is typically ≈0.65 and is always below this floor, so this parameter directly controls prior width. Default 1.5 (95% CI spans ≈exp(±3) ≈ 20× range). Previous default was 1.0 (7× range). Increase to allow Vmax to range more freely; set to 1.0 to restore the old behavior. k_log_sigma_min : float, optional Minimum log-sigma for the K LogNormal prior. Default None, which uses 5*ln(2)/2 ≈ 1.733 (±5 log2FC = 32× range). Increase sparingly — K is already very wide, and wider K worsens the EC50 drift problem for genes where the Hill hasn't saturated within the observed x-range. k_prior_center : str, optional Where to centre the K (EC50) LogNormal prior when NTC cells are absent. Has no effect when NTC cells are present (prior is always centred at the NTC mean). Options: - 'lower' : 5th percentile of x_true guide means. Use when the EC50 is expected near baseline (e.g. strong activators where half-maximum is reached at low cis expression). - 'middle' : half the maximum observed x_true (default, current behaviour). - 'upper' : 95th percentile of x_true guide means. Use when the EC50 is expected near the top of the observed range (e.g. repressors where the effect only kicks in at high cis expression). predictive_checkpoint : str, optional Path to a checkpoint file to use for Predictive sampling only. When set, all prior-computation setup runs as normal (same arguments as the original fit_trans call), but the training loop is skipped and the param_store is loaded from the checkpoint instead. Use this to draw posterior samples from any intermediate checkpoint without re-running training.

**function_type is auto-detected**: every checkpoint stores
``effective_function_type`` — the function that was *actually being
fitted* when that checkpoint was written (``'single_hill'`` during
warmup, the target type afterwards).  ``fit_trans`` reads this value
before initialising the guide, so the guide architecture always matches
the checkpoint.  ``warmup`` is also forced to ``False`` automatically.
You therefore only need to pass ``sum_factor_col`` (and any other
data-access arguments from the original call)::

    model.fit_trans(
        sum_factor_col='sum_factor_adj',
        predictive_checkpoint='outdir/label/trans_checkpoint_gene_warmup.pt',
    )

The same minimal call works for any checkpoint — mid-warmup, post-warmup,
or complete.

To inspect a checkpoint manually::

    import torch
    ckpt = torch.load('trans_checkpoint_gene_step0030000.pt',
                      map_location='cpu', weights_only=False)
    # Was this step in warmup?
    print(ckpt['effective_function_type'])  # 'single_hill' → yes, 'additive_hill' → no
    print(ckpt['phase2_announced'])         # False → in warmup, True → past it

Structural mismatches (N, T, K, C) raise an error; ``distribution``
mismatches produce a warning.

function_type : str Dose-response function: 'single_hill', 'additive_hill', 'polynomial' debug : bool, optional If True, run the slow debug SVI step that checks all parameters for non-finite values at every iteration and prints detailed diagnostics when NaN/Inf are detected. Default False (uses fast svi.step path). Enable when chasing NaN gradients or divergent parameters. **kwargs Additional parameters for specific distributions

Notes

Each modality stores its own fitting results. Primary modality results are also stored at model level as model.posterior_samples_trans. Trans fitting requires that technical fit has been performed for the modality.

If technical_group_code is set (via set_technical_groups()), it will be used for correction. Otherwise, no group correction is applied.

Examples

>>> model.set_technical_groups(['cell_line'])  # Optional, for correction
>>> model.fit_trans(sum_factor_col='sum_factor', function_type='additive_hill')
def set_alpha_x(self, alpha_x, covariates: list[str] = None): 
624    def set_alpha_x(
625        self,
626        alpha_x,
627        covariates: list[str] = None,
628    ):
629        """
630        Set cis-gene overdispersion scaling factors from a pre-fitted or external estimate.
631
632        Stores ``alpha_x`` as a point-estimate tensor of shape ``[C]``, where index 0
633        is the reference group (value fixed to 1.0).  Must be called before
634        ``fit_cis()`` when overdispersion is supplied externally rather than estimated
635        by ``fit_ntc()``.
636
637        Parameters
638        ----------
639        alpha_x : array-like or torch.Tensor
640            Overdispersion scale factors, shape ``[C]`` (including reference group at
641            index 0).  Accepts numpy arrays, lists, or tensors.
642        covariates : list of str, optional
643            Column names in ``meta`` used to define technical groups (e.g.,
644            ``['cell_line']``).  If provided, creates/overwrites
645            ``meta['technical_group_code']``.  If ``None``, assumes
646            ``technical_group_code`` was already set (raises ``ValueError`` if not).
647        """
648        if covariates:
649            if "technical_group_code" in self.meta.columns:
650                warnings.warn("technical_group already set. Overwriting.")
651            self.meta["technical_group_code"] = self.meta.groupby(covariates).ngroup()
652        elif not "technical_group_code" in self.meta.columns:
653            raise ValueError(f"No column 'technical_group_code' found in meta, and no covariates provided.")
654        else:
655            warnings.warn("technical_group previously set. Assuming alpha_x corresponds.")
656        self.alpha_x_prefit = sample_or_use_point("alpha_x_posterior", alpha_x, self.device).flatten()

Set cis-gene overdispersion scaling factors from a pre-fitted or external estimate.

Stores alpha_x as a point-estimate tensor of shape [C], where index 0 is the reference group (value fixed to 1.0). Must be called before fit_cis() when overdispersion is supplied externally rather than estimated by fit_ntc().

Parameters

alpha_x : array-like or torch.Tensor Overdispersion scale factors, shape [C] (including reference group at index 0). Accepts numpy arrays, lists, or tensors. covariates : list of str, optional Column names in meta used to define technical groups (e.g., ['cell_line']). If provided, creates/overwrites meta['technical_group_code']. If None, assumes technical_group_code was already set (raises ValueError if not).

def set_alpha_y(self, alpha_y, covariates: list[str] = None): 
658    def set_alpha_y(
659        self,
660        alpha_y,
661        covariates: list[str] = None,
662    ):
663        """
664        Set trans-gene overdispersion scaling factors from a pre-fitted or external estimate.
665
666        Stores ``alpha_y`` as a point-estimate tensor of shape ``[C, T]`` on the
667        primary modality, where ``C`` is the number of technical groups (index 0 =
668        reference group) and ``T`` is the number of trans features.  Must be called
669        before ``fit_trans()`` when overdispersion is supplied externally rather than
670        estimated by ``fit_ntc()``.
671
672        Parameters
673        ----------
674        alpha_y : array-like or torch.Tensor
675            Overdispersion scale factors, shape ``[C, T]`` (reference group at index 0).
676            Accepts numpy arrays, lists, or tensors.
677        covariates : list of str, optional
678            Column names in ``meta`` used to define technical groups (e.g.,
679            ``['cell_line']``).  If provided, creates/overwrites
680            ``meta['technical_group_code']``.  If ``None``, assumes
681            ``technical_group_code`` was already set (raises ``ValueError`` if not).
682        """
683        if covariates:
684            if "technical_group_code" in self.meta.columns:
685                warnings.warn("technical_group already set. Overwriting.")
686            self.meta["technical_group_code"] = self.meta.groupby(covariates).ngroup()
687        elif not "technical_group_code" in self.meta.columns:
688            raise ValueError(f"No column 'technical_group_code' found in meta, and no covariates provided.")
689        else:
690            warnings.warn("technical_group previously set. Assuming alpha_xy corresponds.")
691
692        # Convert alpha_y to tensor
693        alpha_y = sample_or_use_point("alpha_y_posterior", alpha_y, self.device)
694
695        # Store in primary modality (not model-level)
696        primary_mod = self.get_modality(self.primary_modality)
697        primary_mod.alpha_y_prefit = alpha_y  # Uses property to store in distribution-specific attribute

Set trans-gene overdispersion scaling factors from a pre-fitted or external estimate.

Stores alpha_y as a point-estimate tensor of shape [C, T] on the primary modality, where C is the number of technical groups (index 0 = reference group) and T is the number of trans features. Must be called before fit_trans() when overdispersion is supplied externally rather than estimated by fit_ntc().

If provided, creates/overwrites meta['technical_group_code']. If None, assumes technical_group_code was already set (raises ValueError if not).

def set_x_true(self, x_true): 
699    def set_x_true(
700        self,
701        x_true,
702    ):
703        """
704        Set the posterior cis-gene expression estimate from an external source.
705
706        Stores ``x_true`` as a 1-D point-estimate tensor of shape ``[N]`` (one value
707        per cell, matching ``len(self.meta)``).  Must be called before ``fit_trans()``
708        when ``x_true`` comes from a previously saved fit rather than from running
709        ``fit_cis()`` directly.
710
711        Parameters
712        ----------
713        x_true : array-like or torch.Tensor
714            Posterior mean cis-gene expression, shape ``[N]``.
715            Accepts numpy arrays, lists, or tensors.
716
717        Raises
718        ------
719        ValueError
720            If the provided array does not have exactly ``N`` elements.
721        """
722        N = len(self.meta)
723        x_true = sample_or_use_point("x_true_posterior", x_true, self.device)
724        if not (x_true.ndim == 1 and x_true.shape[0] == N):
725            raise ValueError(
726                f"x_true must have shape N ({N},), but got {x_true.shape}."
727            )
728        self.x_true = x_true

Set the posterior cis-gene expression estimate from an external source.

Stores x_true as a 1-D point-estimate tensor of shape [N] (one value per cell, matching len(self.meta)). Must be called before fit_trans() when x_true comes from a previously saved fit rather than from running fit_cis() directly.

Parameters

x_true : array-like or torch.Tensor Posterior mean cis-gene expression, shape [N]. Accepts numpy arrays, lists, or tensors.

Raises

ValueError If the provided array does not have exactly N elements.

def adjust_ntc_sum_factor( self, sum_factor_col_old: str = 'sum_factor', sum_factor_col_adj: str = 'sum_factor_adj', covariates: list[str] = None): 
731    def adjust_ntc_sum_factor(
732        self,
733        sum_factor_col_old: str = "sum_factor",
734        sum_factor_col_adj: str = "sum_factor_adj",
735        covariates: list[str] = None # Technical group covariates (e.g., ["lane", "cell_line"]) or could be empty
736    ):
737        """
738        Step 1 of sum factor adjustment: Normalize guides to NTC controls.
739
740        Use BEFORE fit_cis() to account for guide-level technical variation.
741        Computes adjustment factor = mean_ntc_sum_factor / mean_guide_sum_factor
742        within covariate groups (e.g., technical groups like cell_line, lane).
743
744        Typical workflow:
745            1. adjust_ntc_sum_factor() -> creates 'sum_factor_adj'
746            2. fit_cis(sum_factor_col='sum_factor_adj')
747            3. refit_sumfactor() -> creates 'sum_factor_refit' (default output name)
748            4. fit_trans(sum_factor_col='sum_factor_refit')
749
750        Parameters
751        ----------
752        sum_factor_col_old : str
753            Name of existing sum factor column in meta (default: 'sum_factor')
754        sum_factor_col_adj : str
755            Name for adjusted sum factor column to create (default: 'sum_factor_adj')
756        covariates : list of str, optional
757            Technical group covariates to group by for adjustment (e.g., ['cell_line', 'lane']).
758            If None or empty, uses global mean across all cells.
759
760        Returns
761        -------
762        None
763            Creates new column sum_factor_col_adj in self.meta
764
765        Notes
766        -----
767        **Single-guide mode** (low MOI): for each guide within each covariate group:
768        - Compute mean NTC sum factor: mean_ntc
769        - Compute mean guide sum factor: mean_guide
770        - Adjustment factor = mean_ntc / mean_guide
771        - Adjusted sum factor = sum_factor * adjustment_factor
772
773        **High MOI mode**: guide effects are assumed additive in log-space (same as fit_cis).
774        For each guide g within each covariate group:
775        - mean_log_sf_g = mean(log(sum_factor)) over cells containing guide g
776        - weighted_NTC = weighted mean of mean_log_sf_g for NTC guides (weights = cells_per_guide)
777        - delta_g = mean_log_sf_g - weighted_NTC
778        For each cell c: log(sf_adj_c) = log(sf_c) - sum(delta_g for guides in cell c)
779        """
780        primary_mod = self.get_modality(self.primary_modality)
781
782        meta_out = self.meta.copy()
783        meta_out["original_index"] = np.arange(len(meta_out))
784
785        # Prefer sum_factors on the modality; fall back to meta for the initial
786        # 'sum_factor' column (present in meta from initialisation).
787        if sum_factor_col_old not in meta_out.columns:
788            if (primary_mod.sum_factors is not None
789                    and sum_factor_col_old in primary_mod.sum_factors.columns):
790                meta_out[sum_factor_col_old] = primary_mod.sum_factors.loc[
791                    meta_out['cell'].values, sum_factor_col_old
792                ].values
793            else:
794                raise ValueError(
795                    f"No column '{sum_factor_col_old}' found in meta or modality sum_factors."
796                )
797
798        # Drop existing adjustment_factor column if it exists (prevents merge conflicts)
799        if "adjustment_factor" in meta_out.columns:
800            meta_out = meta_out.drop(columns=["adjustment_factor"])
801
802        # Make sure all covariates are actually in meta_out
803        if covariates:
804            missing_cols = [c for c in covariates if c not in meta_out.columns]
805            if missing_cols:
806                raise ValueError(
807                    f"Missing covariate columns: {missing_cols}. "
808                    f"Available columns are: {list(meta_out.columns)}"
809            )
810        
811        if self.is_high_moi:
812            # High MOI: guide effects are additive in log-space (same assumption as fit_cis).
813            # For a cell with guides g1, g2: log(sf_adj) = log(sf) - delta_g1 - delta_g2
814            # where delta_g = mean_log_sf_g - weighted_NTC_log_sf (per covariate group).
815            # Weights for NTC mean = cells_per_guide, matching fit_cis.
816
817            guide_assignment = self.guide_assignment  # (n_cells, n_guides)
818
819            # Determine which guides are NTC — works for both guide_meta['target'] and guide_targets_dict
820            _ntc_variants = {'ntc', 'NTC', 'non-targeting', 'non-targeting-control', 'Non-Targeting'}
821            if 'target' in self.guide_meta.columns:
822                is_ntc_guide = self.guide_meta['target'].isin(_ntc_variants).values
823            elif hasattr(self, 'guide_targets_dict') and self.guide_targets_dict:
824                is_ntc_guide = np.array([
825                    any(t in _ntc_variants for t in self.guide_targets_dict.get(row['guide'], []))
826                    for _, row in self.guide_meta.iterrows()
827                ])
828            else:
829                raise ValueError(
830                    "adjust_ntc_sum_factor (high MOI): cannot identify NTC guides — "
831                    "guide_meta has no 'target' column and guide_targets_dict is unavailable."
832                )
833
834            log_sf = np.log(meta_out[sum_factor_col_old].values.astype(float))
835            log_sf_adj = log_sf.copy()
836
837            def _apply_highmoi_correction(pos_indices):
838                ga = guide_assignment[pos_indices]   # (n_sub, n_guides)
839                lsf = log_sf[pos_indices]            # (n_sub,)
840
841                cells_per_guide = ga.sum(axis=0).astype(float)  # (n_guides,)
842
843                # (1) Mean log(sf) per guide via matrix multiply
844                mean_log_sf_g = np.where(
845                    cells_per_guide > 0,
846                    (ga.T @ lsf) / np.maximum(cells_per_guide, 1.0),
847                    np.nan
848                )  # (n_guides,)
849
850                # (2) Weighted NTC mean (weights = cells_per_guide, matching fit_cis)
851                ntc_means = mean_log_sf_g[is_ntc_guide]
852                ntc_counts = cells_per_guide[is_ntc_guide]
853                valid = ~np.isnan(ntc_means) & (ntc_counts > 0)
854                if valid.sum() == 0:
855                    return  # No NTC guides in group; skip correction
856                weighted_NTC_log_sf = np.average(ntc_means[valid], weights=ntc_counts[valid])
857
858                # (3) Per-guide delta; guides with no cells in this group get delta=0
859                delta_g = np.where(~np.isnan(mean_log_sf_g), mean_log_sf_g - weighted_NTC_log_sf, 0.0)
860
861                # (4) Additive correction per cell in log-space
862                log_sf_adj[pos_indices] -= ga @ delta_g
863
864            if not covariates:
865                _apply_highmoi_correction(np.arange(len(meta_out)))
866            else:
867                meta_out["_pos"] = np.arange(len(meta_out))
868                for _, group_df in meta_out.groupby(covariates):
869                    _apply_highmoi_correction(group_df["_pos"].values)
870                meta_out.drop(columns=["_pos"], inplace=True)
871
872            meta_out[sum_factor_col_adj] = np.exp(log_sf_adj)
873
874        elif not covariates:
875            # (1) Mean sum_factor among NTC rows, grouped by covariates (e.g. lane, cell_line)
876            mean_ntc_value = meta_out.loc[meta_out['target'] == 'ntc', sum_factor_col_old].mean()
877
878            # (2) Mean sum_factor among *all* guides, grouped by covariates + [guide_col]
879            df_guide = (
880                meta_out.groupby(["guide_used"])[sum_factor_col_old]
881                .mean()
882                .reset_index(name="mean_SumFacs_guide")
883            )
884
885            # (3) Merge them and compute ratio = mean_NTC / mean_guide
886            df_guide["adjustment_factor"] = (
887                mean_ntc_value / (df_guide["mean_SumFacs_guide"])
888            )
889
890            # (4) Merge that ratio back onto meta_out
891            meta_out = pd.merge(
892                meta_out,
893                df_guide[["guide_used", "adjustment_factor"]],
894                on="guide_used",
895                how="left"
896            )
897
898            # (5) Multiply original sum_factor by ratio
899            meta_out[sum_factor_col_adj] = meta_out[sum_factor_col_old] * meta_out["adjustment_factor"]
900
901        else:
902            # (1) Mean sum_factor among NTC rows, grouped by covariates (e.g. lane, cell_line)
903            df_ntc = (
904                meta_out.loc[meta_out["target"] == "ntc"]
905                .groupby(covariates)[sum_factor_col_old]
906                .mean()
907                .reset_index(name="mean_SumFacs_ntc")
908            )
909
910            # (2) Mean sum_factor among *all* guides, grouped by covariates + [guide_col]
911            df_guide = (
912                meta_out.groupby(covariates + ["guide_used"])[sum_factor_col_old]
913                .mean()
914                .reset_index(name="mean_SumFacs_guide")
915            )
916
917            # (3) Merge them and compute ratio = mean_NTC / mean_guide
918            merged = pd.merge(df_guide, df_ntc, on=covariates, how="left")
919            merged["adjustment_factor"] = merged["mean_SumFacs_ntc"] / merged["mean_SumFacs_guide"]
920
921            # (4) Merge that ratio back onto meta_out
922            merge_cols = covariates + ["guide_used", "adjustment_factor"]
923            meta_out = pd.merge(meta_out, merged[merge_cols], on=covariates + ["guide_used"], how="left")
924
925            # (5) Multiply original sum_factor by ratio
926            meta_out[sum_factor_col_adj] = meta_out[sum_factor_col_old] * meta_out["adjustment_factor"]
927
928        meta_out.sort_values("original_index", inplace=True)
929        meta_out.drop(columns="original_index", inplace=True)
930
931        # Write adjusted sum factor to modality, not back to meta
932        if primary_mod.sum_factors is None:
933            primary_mod.sum_factors = pd.DataFrame(index=meta_out['cell'].values)
934        primary_mod.sum_factors[sum_factor_col_adj] = meta_out.set_index('cell')[sum_factor_col_adj]
935
936        print(f"[INFO] Created '{sum_factor_col_adj}' in modality sum_factors with NTC-based guide-level adjustment.")

Step 1 of sum factor adjustment: Normalize guides to NTC controls.

Use BEFORE fit_cis() to account for guide-level technical variation. Computes adjustment factor = mean_ntc_sum_factor / mean_guide_sum_factor within covariate groups (e.g., technical groups like cell_line, lane).

Typical workflow: 1. adjust_ntc_sum_factor() -> creates 'sum_factor_adj' 2. fit_cis(sum_factor_col='sum_factor_adj') 3. refit_sumfactor() -> creates 'sum_factor_refit' (default output name) 4. fit_trans(sum_factor_col='sum_factor_refit')

Parameters

sum_factor_col_old : str Name of existing sum factor column in meta (default: 'sum_factor') sum_factor_col_adj : str Name for adjusted sum factor column to create (default: 'sum_factor_adj') covariates : list of str, optional Technical group covariates to group by for adjustment (e.g., ['cell_line', 'lane']). If None or empty, uses global mean across all cells.

Returns

None Creates new column sum_factor_col_adj in self.meta

Notes

Single-guide mode (low MOI): for each guide within each covariate group:

  • Compute mean NTC sum factor: mean_ntc
  • Compute mean guide sum factor: mean_guide
  • Adjustment factor = mean_ntc / mean_guide
  • Adjusted sum factor = sum_factor * adjustment_factor

High MOI mode: guide effects are assumed additive in log-space (same as fit_cis). For each guide g within each covariate group:

  • mean_log_sf_g = mean(log(sum_factor)) over cells containing guide g
  • weighted_NTC = weighted mean of mean_log_sf_g for NTC guides (weights = cells_per_guide)
  • delta_g = mean_log_sf_g - weighted_NTC For each cell c: log(sf_adj_c) = log(sf_c) - sum(delta_g for guides in cell c)
def refit_sumfactor( self, sum_factor_col_old: str = 'sum_factor', sum_factor_col_refit: str = 'sum_factor_refit', covariates: list[str] = None, n_knots: int = 5, degree: int = 3, alpha: float = 0.1, use_per_group_splines: bool = None, use_log2: bool = True): 
 938    def refit_sumfactor(
 939        self,
 940        sum_factor_col_old: str = "sum_factor",
 941        sum_factor_col_refit: str = "sum_factor_refit",
 942        covariates: list[str] = None,
 943        n_knots: int = 5,
 944        degree: int = 3,
 945        alpha: float = 0.1,
 946        use_per_group_splines: bool = None,
 947        use_log2: bool = True
 948    ):
 949        """
 950        Step 2 of sum factor adjustment: Remove cis gene contribution.
 951
 952        Use AFTER fit_cis() and BEFORE fit_trans().
 953        Fits a spline regression: (sum_factor - baseline_ntc) ~ f(log2_x_true)
 954        Then removes the predicted x_true contribution from sum factors.
 955
 956        This ensures trans modeling isn't confounded by cis expression levels.
 957
 958        Typical workflow:
 959            1. adjust_ntc_sum_factor() -> creates 'sum_factor_adj'
 960            2. fit_cis(sum_factor_col='sum_factor_adj')
 961            3. refit_sumfactor() -> creates 'sum_factor_refit' (default)  <-- This step
 962            4. fit_trans(sum_factor_col='sum_factor_refit')
 963
 964        Parameters
 965        ----------
 966        sum_factor_col_old : str
 967            Name of existing sum factor column (typically from adjust_ntc_sum_factor)
 968        sum_factor_col_refit : str
 969            Name for refitted sum factor column to create (default: 'sum_factor_refit')
 970        covariates : list of str, optional
 971            Technical group covariates to group by for baseline NTC calculation (e.g., ['cell_line', 'lane'])
 972        n_knots : int
 973            Number of spline knots for regression (default: 5)
 974        degree : int
 975            Polynomial degree of spline pieces (default: 3)
 976        alpha : float
 977            Ridge regression regularization parameter (default: 0.1)
 978        use_per_group_splines : bool, optional
 979            If True, fit separate splines per group and merge them in the overlap region.
 980            If False, use the original algorithm with NTC baseline.
 981            If None (default), auto-detect: use per-group splines if no NTC cells exist.
 982        use_log2 : bool, default True
 983            If True (recommended), use log2(x_true) for the spline regression.
 984            This typically gives better fits since the sum_factor vs x_true relationship
 985            is more linear in log space.
 986
 987        Returns
 988        -------
 989        None
 990            Creates new column sum_factor_col_refit in self.meta
 991
 992        Notes
 993        -----
 994        Algorithm (with NTC):
 995        1. Compute baseline NTC sum factor for each covariate group
 996        2. Compute leftover = sum_factor - baseline_ntc
 997        3. Fit spline model: leftover ~ f(log2_x_true)
 998        4. Predict x_true contribution: y_pred = model(log2_x_true)
 999        5. Adjusted sum factor = max(0, leftover - y_pred + baseline_ntc)
1000
1001        Algorithm (without NTC, per-group splines):
1002        1. Fit separate spline: sum_factor ~ f(log2_x_true) for each group
1003        2. Choose reference group (group with widest x_true range)
1004        3. For other groups, compute offset to align with reference in overlap region
1005        4. Alignment is weighted by density (KDE) in overlap region
1006        5. Apply offsets and compute residuals from aligned splines
1007
1008        Requires:
1009        - self.x_true (or self.log2_x_true) must be set (from fit_cis())
1010        - self.x_true must be set (shape [N], always a point estimate)
1011        """
1012        from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde
1013
1014        primary_mod = self.get_modality(self.primary_modality)
1015
1016        # Read sum factor from modality sum_factors, falling back to meta for the
1017        # initial 'sum_factor' column that was present at model initialisation.
1018        if (primary_mod.sum_factors is not None
1019                and sum_factor_col_old in primary_mod.sum_factors.columns):
1020            sum_factor_data = primary_mod.sum_factors.loc[
1021                self.meta['cell'].values, sum_factor_col_old
1022            ].values.astype(float)  # shape (N,)
1023        elif sum_factor_col_old in self.meta.columns:
1024            sum_factor_data = self.meta[sum_factor_col_old].values.astype(float)
1025        else:
1026            raise ValueError(
1027                f"No column '{sum_factor_col_old}' found in modality sum_factors or meta."
1028            )
1029
1030        if covariates is None:
1031            covariates = []
1032
1033        if covariates:
1034            # Create a single group identifier by concatenating covariate values
1035            tech_group = self.meta[covariates].astype(str).agg('_'.join, axis=1)
1036            groups, group_id = np.unique(tech_group, return_inverse=True)
1037            n_groups = len(groups)
1038        else:
1039            # No grouping, treat all samples as a single group
1040            groups, group_id = np.array(["all"]), np.zeros(len(self.meta), dtype=int)
1041            n_groups = 1
1042
1043        # Get x_true values (optionally in log2 space); x_true is always [N] point estimate
1044        if use_log2:
1045            if hasattr(self, 'log2_x_true') and self.log2_x_true is not None:
1046                X_true = self.log2_x_true.cpu().numpy() if hasattr(self.log2_x_true, 'cpu') else np.array(self.log2_x_true)
1047            else:
1048                x_raw = self.x_true.cpu().numpy() if hasattr(self.x_true, 'cpu') else np.array(self.x_true)
1049                X_true = np.log2(np.maximum(x_raw, 1e-6))
1050            print(f"[INFO] Using log2(x_true) for spline fitting (range: [{X_true.min():.2f}, {X_true.max():.2f}])")
1051        else:
1052            X_true = self.x_true.cpu().numpy() if hasattr(self.x_true, 'cpu') else np.array(self.x_true)
1053            print(f"[INFO] Using x_true (linear scale) for spline fitting (range: [{X_true.min():.2f}, {X_true.max():.2f}])")
1054
1055        # Check if we have NTC cells
1056        has_ntc = 'target' in self.meta.columns and (self.meta['target'] == 'ntc').any()
1057
1058        # Auto-detect whether to use per-group splines
1059        if use_per_group_splines is None:
1060            use_per_group_splines = not has_ntc and n_groups > 1
1061            if use_per_group_splines:
1062                print(f"[INFO] No NTC cells detected with {n_groups} groups. Using per-group spline alignment.")
1063
1064        if use_per_group_splines and n_groups > 1:
1065            # =========================================================================
1066            # Per-group spline fitting with density-weighted alignment
1067            # =========================================================================
1068
1069            # Step 1: Fit separate splines for each group
1070            group_models = {}
1071            group_x_ranges = {}
1072
1073            for grp_idx, grp_name in enumerate(groups):
1074                mask = (group_id == grp_idx)
1075                x_grp = X_true[mask]
1076                y_grp = sum_factor_data[mask]
1077
1078                if len(x_grp) < 10:
1079                    print(f"[WARN] Group '{grp_name}' has only {len(x_grp)} cells, skipping spline fit")
1080                    continue
1081
1082                model = make_pipeline(
1083                    SplineTransformer(n_knots=n_knots, degree=degree),
1084                    Ridge(alpha=alpha)
1085                )
1086                model.fit(x_grp.reshape(-1, 1), y_grp)
1087
1088                group_models[grp_idx] = model
1089                group_x_ranges[grp_idx] = (x_grp.min(), x_grp.max())
1090
1091                print(f"[INFO] Fitted spline for group '{grp_name}': x_true range [{x_grp.min():.2f}, {x_grp.max():.2f}]")
1092
1093            if len(group_models) < 2:
1094                print(f"[WARN] Only {len(group_models)} group(s) with enough cells. Falling back to global spline.")
1095                use_per_group_splines = False
1096            else:
1097                # Step 2: Choose reference group (widest x_true range)
1098                ref_grp = max(group_x_ranges.keys(), key=lambda g: group_x_ranges[g][1] - group_x_ranges[g][0])
1099                ref_name = groups[ref_grp]
1100                print(f"[INFO] Reference group: '{ref_name}' (widest x_true range)")
1101
1102                # Step 3: Compute offsets for other groups
1103                group_offsets = {ref_grp: 0.0}
1104
1105                for grp_idx in group_models:
1106                    if grp_idx == ref_grp:
1107                        continue
1108
1109                    grp_name = groups[grp_idx]
1110
1111                    # Find overlap region
1112                    ref_min, ref_max = group_x_ranges[ref_grp]
1113                    grp_min, grp_max = group_x_ranges[grp_idx]
1114
1115                    overlap_min = max(ref_min, grp_min)
1116                    overlap_max = min(ref_max, grp_max)
1117
1118                    if overlap_min >= overlap_max:
1119                        print(f"[WARN] No overlap between '{ref_name}' and '{grp_name}'. Using median offset.")
1120                        # Fallback: use median difference at closest points
1121                        ref_mask = (group_id == ref_grp)
1122                        grp_mask = (group_id == grp_idx)
1123                        offset = np.median(sum_factor_data[ref_mask]) - np.median(sum_factor_data[grp_mask])
1124                        group_offsets[grp_idx] = offset
1125                        continue
1126
1127                    # Create evaluation grid in overlap region
1128                    x_eval = np.linspace(overlap_min, overlap_max, 100)
1129
1130                    # Predict from both splines
1131                    y_ref = group_models[ref_grp].predict(x_eval.reshape(-1, 1))
1132                    y_grp = group_models[grp_idx].predict(x_eval.reshape(-1, 1))
1133
1134                    # Compute density weights using KDE
1135                    ref_mask = (group_id == ref_grp)
1136                    grp_mask = (group_id == grp_idx)
1137
1138                    x_ref_data = X_true[ref_mask]
1139                    x_grp_data = X_true[grp_mask]
1140
1141                    # Filter to overlap region for KDE
1142                    x_ref_overlap = x_ref_data[(x_ref_data >= overlap_min) & (x_ref_data <= overlap_max)]
1143                    x_grp_overlap = x_grp_data[(x_grp_data >= overlap_min) & (x_grp_data <= overlap_max)]
1144
1145                    if len(x_ref_overlap) < 5 or len(x_grp_overlap) < 5:
1146                        print(f"[WARN] Sparse overlap between '{ref_name}' and '{grp_name}'. Using uniform weights.")
1147                        weights = np.ones(len(x_eval))
1148                    else:
1149                        # KDE for both groups
1150                        try:
1151                            kde_ref = gaussian_kde(x_ref_overlap)
1152                            kde_grp = gaussian_kde(x_grp_overlap)
1153
1154                            # Combined density (geometric mean)
1155                            density_ref = kde_ref(x_eval)
1156                            density_grp = kde_grp(x_eval)
1157                            weights = np.sqrt(density_ref * density_grp)
1158                            weights = weights / weights.sum()  # Normalize
1159                        except Exception as e:
1160                            print(f"[WARN] KDE failed for '{grp_name}': {e}. Using uniform weights.")
1161                            weights = np.ones(len(x_eval)) / len(x_eval)
1162
1163                    # Compute weighted offset: minimize sum(w * (y_ref - (y_grp + offset))^2)
1164                    # Optimal offset = sum(w * (y_ref - y_grp)) / sum(w)
1165                    offset = np.sum(weights * (y_ref - y_grp)) / np.sum(weights)
1166                    group_offsets[grp_idx] = offset
1167
1168                    print(f"[INFO] Offset for group '{grp_name}': {offset:.4f} (overlap: [{overlap_min:.2f}, {overlap_max:.2f}])")
1169
1170                # Step 4: Compute predictions with offsets
1171                y_pred = np.zeros(len(X_true))
1172
1173                for grp_idx in group_models:
1174                    mask = (group_id == grp_idx)
1175                    x_grp = X_true[mask]
1176
1177                    # Predict and add offset
1178                    pred = group_models[grp_idx].predict(x_grp.reshape(-1, 1))
1179                    pred_aligned = pred + group_offsets[grp_idx]
1180                    y_pred[mask] = pred_aligned
1181
1182                # Handle any groups without models (too few cells)
1183                missing_mask = np.zeros(len(X_true), dtype=bool)
1184                for grp_idx in range(n_groups):
1185                    if grp_idx not in group_models:
1186                        missing_mask |= (group_id == grp_idx)
1187
1188                if missing_mask.any():
1189                    # Use reference group's model for missing groups
1190                    y_pred[missing_mask] = group_models[ref_grp].predict(X_true[missing_mask].reshape(-1, 1))
1191
1192                # Compute residuals (sum_factor - predicted trend)
1193                residuals = sum_factor_data - y_pred
1194
1195                # The adjusted sum factor removes the x_true-dependent trend
1196                # We want to keep the baseline level, so add back the global mean predicted value
1197                global_baseline = np.mean(y_pred)
1198                adjusted = residuals + global_baseline
1199
1200                # Clamp to a small positive floor rather than 0 to prevent mu_final=0 in
1201                # trans fitting (log(0) = -inf logits → NaN gradients).
1202                # Floor = 1% of the minimum positive sum factor in the data.
1203                sf_min_positive = sum_factor_data[sum_factor_data > 0].min() if (sum_factor_data > 0).any() else 1e-6
1204                sf_floor = 0.01 * sf_min_positive
1205                n_clamped = int((adjusted < sf_floor).sum())
1206                if n_clamped > 0:
1207                    print(f"[WARNING] refit_sumfactor: {n_clamped} cell(s) had adjusted sum factor "
1208                          f"below floor ({sf_floor:.4g}); clamped to floor. "
1209                          f"This can happen when the spline overpredicts the cis-gene contribution. "
1210                          f"These cells will have near-zero library size in trans fitting.")
1211                if primary_mod.sum_factors is None:
1212                    primary_mod.sum_factors = pd.DataFrame(index=self.meta['cell'].values)
1213                primary_mod.sum_factors[sum_factor_col_refit] = np.maximum(sf_floor, adjusted)
1214
1215                print(f"[INFO] Created '{sum_factor_col_refit}' in modality sum_factors using per-group spline alignment.")
1216                return
1217
1218        # =========================================================================
1219        # Original algorithm: NTC-based baseline subtraction
1220        # =========================================================================
1221        baseline_ntc_of_group = np.zeros(n_groups)
1222        if covariates:
1223            for grp, grp_name in enumerate(groups):
1224                mask_grp = (tech_group == grp_name)
1225                # Among that group, pick rows with target == 'ntc'
1226                if 'target' in self.meta.columns:
1227                    mask_ntc = (self.meta['target'] == 'ntc') & mask_grp
1228                else:
1229                    mask_ntc = np.zeros(len(self.meta), dtype=bool)
1230
1231                # If a group has no NTC, use fallback
1232                if not np.any(mask_ntc):
1233                    baseline_ntc_of_group[grp] = 1.0  # fallback
1234                else:
1235                    baseline_ntc_of_group[grp] = np.mean(sum_factor_data[mask_ntc])
1236        else:
1237            grp = 0
1238            if 'target' in self.meta.columns:
1239                mask_ntc = (self.meta['target'] == 'ntc')
1240            else:
1241                mask_ntc = np.zeros(len(self.meta), dtype=bool)
1242
1243            if not np.any(mask_ntc):
1244                baseline_ntc_of_group[grp] = 1.0  # fallback
1245            else:
1246                baseline_ntc_of_group[grp] = np.mean(sum_factor_data[mask_ntc])
1247
1248        # leftover_data[i] = sum_factor[i] - baseline_ntc_of_group[group_id[i]]
1249        leftover_data = sum_factor_data - baseline_ntc_of_group[group_id]
1250
1251        # Build spline + ridge pipeline
1252        model_spline_ridge = make_pipeline(
1253            SplineTransformer(n_knots=n_knots, degree=degree),
1254            Ridge(alpha=alpha)
1255        )
1256
1257        # Fit the model
1258        model_spline_ridge.fit(X_true.reshape(-1, 1), leftover_data)
1259
1260        # Predict and adjust
1261        y_pred = model_spline_ridge.predict(X_true.reshape(-1, 1))
1262        adjusted = leftover_data - y_pred + baseline_ntc_of_group[group_id]
1263
1264        # Clamp to a small positive floor rather than 0 to prevent mu_final=0 in
1265        # trans fitting (log(0) = -inf logits → NaN gradients).
1266        # Floor = 1% of the minimum positive sum factor in the data.
1267        sf_min_positive = sum_factor_data[sum_factor_data > 0].min() if (sum_factor_data > 0).any() else 1e-6
1268        sf_floor = 0.01 * sf_min_positive
1269        n_clamped = int((adjusted < sf_floor).sum())
1270        if n_clamped > 0:
1271            print(f"[WARNING] refit_sumfactor: {n_clamped} cell(s) had adjusted sum factor "
1272                  f"below floor ({sf_floor:.4g}); clamped to floor. "
1273                  f"This can happen when the spline overpredicts the cis-gene contribution. "
1274                  f"These cells will have near-zero library size in trans fitting.")
1275        if primary_mod.sum_factors is None:
1276            primary_mod.sum_factors = pd.DataFrame(index=self.meta['cell'].values)
1277        primary_mod.sum_factors[sum_factor_col_refit] = np.maximum(sf_floor, adjusted)
1278        print(f"[INFO] Created '{sum_factor_col_refit}' in modality sum_factors with x_true-based adjustment.")

Step 2 of sum factor adjustment: Remove cis gene contribution.

Use AFTER fit_cis() and BEFORE fit_trans(). Fits a spline regression: (sum_factor - baseline_ntc) ~ f(log2_x_true) Then removes the predicted x_true contribution from sum factors.

This ensures trans modeling isn't confounded by cis expression levels.

Typical workflow: 1. adjust_ntc_sum_factor() -> creates 'sum_factor_adj' 2. fit_cis(sum_factor_col='sum_factor_adj') 3. refit_sumfactor() -> creates 'sum_factor_refit' (default) <-- This step 4. fit_trans(sum_factor_col='sum_factor_refit')

Parameters

sum_factor_col_old : str Name of existing sum factor column (typically from adjust_ntc_sum_factor) sum_factor_col_refit : str Name for refitted sum factor column to create (default: 'sum_factor_refit') covariates : list of str, optional Technical group covariates to group by for baseline NTC calculation (e.g., ['cell_line', 'lane']) n_knots : int Number of spline knots for regression (default: 5) degree : int Polynomial degree of spline pieces (default: 3) alpha : float Ridge regression regularization parameter (default: 0.1) use_per_group_splines : bool, optional If True, fit separate splines per group and merge them in the overlap region. If False, use the original algorithm with NTC baseline. If None (default), auto-detect: use per-group splines if no NTC cells exist. use_log2 : bool, default True If True (recommended), use log2(x_true) for the spline regression. This typically gives better fits since the sum_factor vs x_true relationship is more linear in log space.

Returns

None Creates new column sum_factor_col_refit in self.meta

Notes

Algorithm (with NTC):

  1. Compute baseline NTC sum factor for each covariate group
  2. Compute leftover = sum_factor - baseline_ntc
  3. Fit spline model: leftover ~ f(log2_x_true)
  4. Predict x_true contribution: y_pred = model(log2_x_true)
  5. Adjusted sum factor = max(0, leftover - y_pred + baseline_ntc)

Algorithm (without NTC, per-group splines):

  1. Fit separate spline: sum_factor ~ f(log2_x_true) for each group
  2. Choose reference group (group with widest x_true range)
  3. For other groups, compute offset to align with reference in overlap region
  4. Alignment is weighted by density (KDE) in overlap region
  5. Apply offsets and compute residuals from aligned splines

Requires:

  • self.x_true (or self.log2_x_true) must be set (from fit_cis())
  • self.x_true must be set (shape [N], always a point estimate)
def subset_cells( self, cell_mask: Union[numpy.ndarray, pandas.core.series.Series, list] = None, query: str = None, preserve_fits: bool = True): 
1373    def subset_cells(
1374        self,
1375        cell_mask: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, list] = None,
1376        query: str = None,
1377        preserve_fits: bool = True

1379        """
1380        Create a new model instance with a subset of cells.
1381

1383        technical group (e.g., one cell line only).
1384
1385        Parameters
1386        ----------
1387        cell_mask : np.ndarray, pd.Series, or list, optional

1397        -------
1398        bayesDREAM

1400
1401        Examples
1402        --------
1403        # Subset by query
1404        model_k562 = model.subset_cells(query="cell_line == 'K562'")
1405
1406        # Subset by mask
1407        mask = model.meta['cell_line'].str.contains('K562')
1408        model_k562 = model.subset_cells(cell_mask=mask)
1409
1410        # Subset by cell list
1411        cells = model.meta[model.meta['cell_line'] == 'K562']['cell'].tolist()
1412        model_k562 = model.subset_cells(cell_mask=cells)

1414        if cell_mask is None and query is None:
1415            raise ValueError("Must provide either cell_mask or query")
1416
1417        if query is not None:
1418            # Filter meta using query
1419            meta_subset = self.meta.query(query).copy()
1420            cells_to_keep = meta_subset['cell'].values
1421        elif isinstance(cell_mask, (list, np.ndarray, pd.Series)):
1422            # Handle list of cell names
1423            if isinstance(cell_mask, list) and len(cell_mask) > 0 and isinstance(cell_mask[0], str):
1424                cells_to_keep = cell_mask
1425                meta_subset = self.meta[self.meta['cell'].isin(cells_to_keep)].copy()
1426            # Handle boolean mask
1427            elif isinstance(cell_mask, (np.ndarray, pd.Series)):
1428                if cell_mask.dtype == bool:
1429                    meta_subset = self.meta[cell_mask].copy()
1430                    cells_to_keep = meta_subset['cell'].values
1431                else:
1432                    # Assume it's a list of cell names
1433                    cells_to_keep = cell_mask
1434                    meta_subset = self.meta[self.meta['cell'].isin(cells_to_keep)].copy()
1435            else:
1436                raise ValueError("cell_mask must be boolean array/Series or list of cell names")
1437        else:
1438            raise ValueError("Invalid cell_mask type")
1439
1440        if len(meta_subset) == 0:
1441            raise ValueError("Subset resulted in zero cells")
1442
1443        print(f"[INFO] Subsetting from {len(self.meta)} to {len(meta_subset)} cells")
1444
1445        # Subset counts — reconstruct from modalities (self.counts is None after init)
1446        cells_to_keep_set = set(cells_to_keep)
1447        gene_mod = self.get_modality(self.primary_modality)
1448        cis_mod  = self.get_modality('cis') if 'cis' in self.modalities else None
1449
1450        # Get column indices in the gene modality matching cells_to_keep
1451        if gene_mod.cell_names:
1452            gene_cell_indices = [i for i, c in enumerate(gene_mod.cell_names) if c in cells_to_keep_set]
1453        else:
1454            gene_cell_indices = [i for i, cell in enumerate(self.meta['cell']) if cell in cells_to_keep_set]
1455
1456        gene_counts_sub  = gene_mod.counts[:, gene_cell_indices]
1457        gene_feat_meta   = gene_mod.feature_meta.copy() if gene_mod.feature_meta is not None else None
1458
1459        if cis_mod is not None:
1460            if cis_mod.cell_names:
1461                cis_cell_indices = [i for i, c in enumerate(cis_mod.cell_names) if c in cells_to_keep_set]
1462            else:
1463                cis_cell_indices = gene_cell_indices
1464
1465            cis_counts_row = cis_mod.counts[:, cis_cell_indices]   # shape [1, N_sub]
1466            cis_feat_meta  = cis_mod.feature_meta.copy()
1467
1468            # Stack: cis row first (row 0), then gene rows
1469            if sparse.issparse(gene_counts_sub):
1470                cis_sp       = (cis_counts_row.tocsr() if sparse.issparse(cis_counts_row)
1471                                else sparse.csr_matrix(np.asarray(cis_counts_row).reshape(1, -1)))
1472                counts_subset = sparse.vstack([cis_sp, gene_counts_sub], format='csr')
1473            else:
1474                cis_dense     = np.asarray(cis_counts_row).reshape(1, -1)
1475                counts_subset = np.vstack([cis_dense, np.asarray(gene_counts_sub)])
1476
1477            # Build combined feature_meta with sequential 0-based index
1478            # (constructor's _extract_cis_from_gene searches this by value, not position)
1479            cis_fm  = cis_feat_meta.copy();  cis_fm.index  = [0]
1480            if gene_feat_meta is not None:
1481                gene_fm = gene_feat_meta.copy(); gene_fm.index = range(1, 1 + len(gene_feat_meta))
1482                feature_meta_subset = pd.concat([cis_fm, gene_fm], ignore_index=True)
1483            else:
1484                feature_meta_subset = cis_fm
1485        else:
1486            counts_subset       = gene_counts_sub
1487            feature_meta_subset = gene_feat_meta
1488
1489        # Subset high MOI guide_assignment if applicable
1490        guide_assignment_subset = None
1491        if self.is_high_moi:
1492            # Get indices of subsetted cells in original meta
1493            cell_indices = [i for i, cell in enumerate(self.meta['cell']) if cell in cells_to_keep]
1494            guide_assignment_subset = self.guide_assignment[cell_indices, :]
1495
1496        # Create new model instance
1497        from .model import bayesDREAM
1498
1499        # For high MOI mode, reconstruct guide_target DataFrame from guide_targets_dict
1500        # This preserves many-to-many guide-target relationships
1501        guide_target_df = None
1502        if self.is_high_moi and hasattr(self, 'guide_targets_dict') and self.guide_targets_dict:
1503            guide_target_rows = []
1504            for guide, targets in self.guide_targets_dict.items():
1505                for target in targets:
1506                    guide_target_rows.append({'guide': guide, 'target': target})
1507            if guide_target_rows:
1508                guide_target_df = pd.DataFrame(guide_target_rows)
1509
1510        model_new = bayesDREAM(
1511            meta=meta_subset,
1512            counts=counts_subset,
1513            modality_name=self.primary_modality,  # Use same primary modality name
1514            feature_meta=feature_meta_subset,
1515            cis_gene=self.cis_gene,
1516            guide_covariates=self.guide_covariates,  # Preserve guide covariates
1517            guide_covariates_ntc=self.guide_covariates_ntc,  # Preserve NTC guide covariates
1518            output_dir=self.output_dir,
1519            label=f"{self.label}_subset",
1520            device=str(self.device),
1521            random_seed=2402,
1522            cores=1,
1523            guide_assignment=guide_assignment_subset,
1524            guide_meta=self.guide_meta.copy() if self.is_high_moi else None,
1525            guide_target=guide_target_df,  # Preserve many-to-many guide-target relationships
1526            require_ntc=False  # Allow subsetting without NTC cells
1527        )
1528
1529
1530        # Copy additional modalities (beyond the primary 'gene' modality)
1531        if hasattr(self, 'modalities'):
1532            for mod_name, modality in self.modalities.items():
1533                if mod_name not in ['gene', 'cis']:  # Skip primary and cis modalities (already handled)
1534                    # Subset the modality to the selected cells using cell names
1535                    subset_modality = modality.get_cell_subset(cells_to_keep)
1536                    model_new.modalities[mod_name] = subset_modality
1537            print(f"[INFO] Copied {len(self.modalities) - 2} additional modalities to subset model")
1538
1539        # Optionally preserve fitted parameters
1540        if preserve_fits:
1541            # Copy technical fit parameters if they exist
1542            if self.alpha_x_prefit is not None:
1543                model_new.alpha_x_prefit = self.alpha_x_prefit.clone() if isinstance(self.alpha_x_prefit, torch.Tensor) else self.alpha_x_prefit
1544
1545            # Copy all fit attributes from original modalities to new modalities
1546            # (including 'gene' and 'cis' which were recreated during initialization)
1547            # NOTE: alpha_y_prefit is stored per-modality as a [C, T] mean point estimate
1548
1549            # Helper to clone tensors
1550            def _clone_attr(val):
1551                if hasattr(val, 'clone'):
1552                    return val.clone()
1553                return val
1554
1555            # Modality-level attributes to copy from fit_technical and fit_trans
1556            # NOTE: alpha_y_prefit is a property, not an attribute - it derives from _mult/_add
1557            modality_attrs = [
1558                'alpha_y_prefit_mult', 'alpha_y_prefit_add',
1559                'posterior_samples_ntc', 'posterior_samples_trans', 'losses_trans'
1560            ]
1561            for mod_name in self.modalities:
1562                if mod_name in model_new.modalities:
1563                    orig_mod = self.modalities[mod_name]
1564                    new_mod = model_new.modalities[mod_name]
1565                    copied_attrs = []
1566                    for attr in modality_attrs:
1567                        orig_val = getattr(orig_mod, attr, None)
1568                        if orig_val is not None:
1569                            setattr(new_mod, attr, _clone_attr(orig_val))
1570                            copied_attrs.append(attr)
1571                    if copied_attrs:
1572                        print(f"[INFO] Copied {copied_attrs} from '{mod_name}' modality")
1573                    else:
1574                        print(f"[DEBUG] No attributes to copy from '{mod_name}' modality")
1575                        # Debug: show which attrs exist
1576                        for attr in modality_attrs:
1577                            val = getattr(orig_mod, attr, "MISSING")
1578                            print(f"  {attr}: {type(val).__name__ if val != 'MISSING' else 'MISSING'}")
1579                else:
1580                    print(f"[WARN] Modality '{mod_name}' not found in new model")
1581
1582            # Copy cis fit parameters if they exist
1583            # Get cell indices for subsetting cell-indexed tensors
1584            cell_indices_torch = torch.tensor(
1585                [i for i, cell in enumerate(self.meta['cell']) if cell in cells_to_keep],
1586                dtype=torch.long
1587            )
1588
1589            if hasattr(self, 'x_true') and self.x_true is not None:
1590                # x_true is always shape [N] - subset to new cells
1591                if isinstance(self.x_true, torch.Tensor):
